title: Acta Marine completes four vessel CSOV newbuild programme
content:
Acta Marine has announced the delivery of its latest next-generation Walk-to-Work
(W2W) DP2 Construction Service Operation Vessel (CSOV), Acta Aquarius,
following Acta Pegasus, Acta Hercules and Acta Gemini. Acta Marine confirmed
this is the final vessel in the series.
Rob Boer, CEO of Acta Marine, commented: "The delivery of Acta Aquarius
is a proud moment for Acta Marine and marks the completion of our four
vessel newbuild programme with Tersan Shipyard."
Adding: "These vessels represent an important investment in the future
of our fleet and strengthen our ability to support our clients in the offshore
wind industry."
The new vessel is powered by dual-fuel methanol, supporting lower-emission
operations. According to the company, it also features a telescopic motion
compensated gangway and a 3D motion compensated crane.
According to the announcement, Acta Marine will look to deploy the vessel
in support of offshore wind operations.

title: IX Renewables and TWD sign agreement to support Taiwan’s offshore wind development
content:
IX Renewables and TWD sign agreement to support Taiwan’s offshore wind development TGS 4C | 4C Offshore News
IX Renewables and TWD sign agreement to support Taiwan’s offshore wind development
IX Renewables and TWD have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) aimed
at creating a strategic framework to support offshore wind developments
in Taiwan and the wider Asia Pacific (APAC) region.
The agreement reinforces the companies' long-standing relationship and
outlines a collaborative approach to future offshore wind projects. According
to the announcement, the partnership will combine IX Renewables' EPCI management
capabilities with TWD's engineering and construction expertise, enabling
the companies to address project challenges while maximising efficiency.
"Our cooperation with TWD has already demonstrated the value of bringing
project execution experience and engineering expertise together,"
said Eric Kamphues, CEO of IX Renewables.
The partnership comes as Taiwan continues to advance its offshore wind
sector through the launch of its Round 3.3 auction process and the proposed
framework for floating offshore wind development.
According to the companies, this growth in the offshore wind market is
driving demand for both fixed-bottom and floating wind expertise, supported
partners and financial institutions.
"We are glad to have a strategic partner that is invested in Taiwan's
offshore wind industry and helps move projects forward in a complex stakeholder
landscape," said Christos Charalambous, Country Manager of TWD Taiwan.
"It is reassuring to see both IX Renewables and TWD present in the
market, committed and ready to help deliver a greener future."

title: JFE Engineering and Akita Maritime Service secure offshore maintenance contract
content:
JFE Engineering and Akita Maritime Service have formed a joint venture
that has been awarded a contract to provide inspection and maintenance
services for the balance of plant (BOP) infrastructure at the offshore
wind project located off the coast of Oga City, Katagami City and Akita
The scope covers the onshore substation, onshore transmission lines, submarine
cables and monopile foundations. The initial contract will run for five
years, with the companies expected to support the assets throughout the
project's operating life through contract extensions and renewals.
The offshore wind farm is scheduled to begin operations in June 2028 and
is set to be the first project commissioned under Japan's offshore wind
development framework established under the Renewable Energy Sea Area Use
JFE Engineering said the award builds on its experience in wind farm EPC
and maintenance services, as well as its role manufacturing and transporting
monopile foundations.
According to the announcement Akita Maritime Service will provide support
including transmission line inspections and vessel coordination for maintenance
activities.

title: SSEN Transmission successfully uses drones to install DLR technology
content:
SSEN Transmission has announced the successful use of a drone to install
Dynamic Line Rating (DLR) technology on a live transmission conductor,
marking a milestone as the first company in the UK to complete the process.
an outage or physical access to the line.
According to the announcement, the method will help maximise network capacity,
as DLR uses real-time environmental conditions to calculate how much electricity
a transmission line can safely carry, rather than relying on predetermined
seasonal limits.
Niall McDonald, SSEN Transmission Project Director, said: “This approach
has the potential to make it easier and more flexible to deploy DLR across
our network, helping us make better use of existing capacity and move more
renewable electricity through the system.”
Martin Queen, Chief Engineer at Ofgem, the energy regulator, said: “A
live-line installation is exceptionally important because it allows us
to avoid system outages, which are becoming increasingly difficult to accommodate
on a highly constrained network.”

title: Seaway 7 installs first inter-array cable at Hornsea 3 offshore wind farm
content:
Seaway 7 has announced the installation of the first inter-array cable
for the 2.9 GW Hornsea
3 offshore wind farm.
The Ørsted led project is located 120 km off the Norfolk coast and will
generate enough renewable electricity to power an estimated 3.3 million
UK households.
The company will carry out the transport and installation of 536 km of
66 kV inter-array cables, helping connect the wind farm's 231 offshore
wind turbines to the offshore converter station.
According to the announcement, Seaway 7's work on the Hornsea 3 project
continues its long-term relationship with Ørsted, following their involvement
in the 1.2 GW Hornsea 1 and 1.3 GW Hornsea 2 offshore wind farms.

title: Semco Maritime and PTSC M&C awarded offshore substation supply contract for Fengmiao II
content:
Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners has announced that the Fengmiao II offshore
wind project has signed an offshore substation supply contract with Semco
Maritime and PTSC Mechanical & Construction (PTSC M&C).
Fengmiao II is being developed by Copenhagen Offshore Partners. The 600
MW offshore wind project is located 40 kilometres off the coast of Taichung
City, Taiwan.
According to the announcement, the contract covers the engineering, procurement,
fabrication and installation of the offshore substation.
The engineering, procurement and installation of the substation's electrical
systems have been awarded to Semco Maritime, while PTSC M&C will fabricate
the offshore substation's structural components.
Mark Wainwright, CEO of the Fengmiao II Offshore Wind Project, said: "Through
our collaboration on Fengmiao I, both teams have established a strong working
relationship and a high level of mutual understanding while gaining valuable
engineering experience."
Adding: "These achievements provide a solid foundation for the successful
delivery of the Fengmiao II offshore substation."
Naiwen Marina Hsu, president of CIP Asia-Pacific, said: "Fengmiao
II will build on the success of Fengmiao I by continuing to leverage its
proven development model, with financial close targeted by the end of the
second quarter of 2027."

title: BYD weighs battery plant in Portugal - Batteries News
content:
BYD weighs battery plant in Portugal
BYD is considering a battery plant in Portugal, with Matosinhos among the possible sites, in a potential boost to the country’s electric vehicle supply chain.
Chinese carmaker BYD is considering building an electric vehicle battery plant in Portugal, with the former Galp refinery site in Matosinhos among the possible locations. The project could strengthen Portugal’s role in the Iberian electric mobility supply chain.
According to the Expresso newspaper, BYD has been in talks with the Portuguese government and AICEP, the country’s trade and investment agency, about the investment. Matosinhos mayor Luísa Salgueiro said such an investment would be “a very welcome project”, although the municipality has not yet been formally contacted.
Of the 240 hectares occupied by the former refinery, 100 have been transferred to the municipality, with 40 earmarked for a University of Porto hub and 20 for a green park. The remaining area still has no defined use.
The location could benefit from its proximity to the future Barroso lithium mine in Boticas, whose production is expected to start in 2028, as well as access to the port of Leixões and major transport links. The plant could serve as an Iberian battery production hub, including for BYD’s future car factory expected to be located in Spain.
Portugal’s Economy Ministry and AICEP have been supporting the project for some time. Economy Minister Castro Almeida has acknowledged a “fruitful dialogue” with a Chinese carmaker about setting up a unit in Portugal, but declined to give further details.

title: CATL is exploring an air-breathing battery. Could it give EVs 2,000 km of range? - Batteries News
content:
CATL is exploring an air-breathing battery. Could it give EVs 2,000 km of range?
A report by Chinese technology outlet
has revived claims that lithium-air batteries could deliver electric vehicle ranges of up to 2,000 km and achieve five times the energy density of
solid-state
batteries
. The chemistry’s theoretical specific energy is often cited at around 3,505 Wh/kg. However, this figure describes electrochemical potential, not the performance of a complete automotive
connection comes from Chief Scientist Wu Kai, who identified lithium-air technology as a long-term research direction at the 2026 Equipment Powerhouse Forum. As
we previously reported
, CATL’s broader battery roadmap places sodium-ion and all-solid-state technologies closer to commercialisation, while lithium-air remains a longer-term research prospect. CATL has not announced a 2,000 km production-car target or a commercial launch schedule for the technology.
The gap between theoretical energy density and automotive performance remains substantial. Oxygen management, chemical stability, rechargeability and the supporting equipment all present significant engineering challenges.
How lithium-air batteries work
Conventional lithium-ion batteries store lithium within two electrodes, with lithium ions moving between the anode and cathode during charging and discharging. Lithium-air batteries instead use metallic lithium as the negative electrode and oxygen from the surrounding environment as the positive reactant.
During discharge, lithium reacts with oxygen to form lithium peroxide (Li₂O₂) inside a porous cathode. Charging reverses the reaction, releasing oxygen and returning lithium ions to the anode. Drawing oxygen from outside the cell rather than storing the positive reactant in a conventional cathode material gives the chemistry high theoretical specific energy.
The frequently cited 3,505 Wh/kg figure relates to the theoretical lithium-peroxide reaction and includes the oxygen reactant mass. Higher figures approaching 12,000 Wh/kg use a different calculation boundary that excludes oxygen mass. Neither represents the energy density of a complete automotive battery. Electrolytes, electrodes, protective components and air-management equipment all add weight and volume.
Laboratory progress has not solved the durability problem
Automotive interest in lithium-air batteries predates CATL’s research. IBM launched its Battery 500 project in 2009, targeting a metal-air battery capable of powering an electric car for 500 miles (805 km) on a charge. The multinational research programme involved academic and industry partners but did not produce a commercially available automotive battery.
More recent research has addressed lithium-air batteries’ chemical limitations, particularly the accumulation of discharge products inside porous cathodes. A
2025 study by researchers at the University of Science and Technology of China
, including Professor Peng Tan, examined how electrolyte oxygen-transport properties influence reaction mechanisms in lithium-oxygen batteries. Using thick electrodes, the researchers showed how mass-transfer resistance can change reaction pathways at different positions within an electrode. The work provides insight into electrode design but does not establish an automotive solution to cathode blockage.
A separate result came from researchers associated with Jilin University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences. A
2024 study published in
Advanced Energy Materials
reported an optimised lithium-air pouch-cell configuration achieving 757.5 Wh/kg with an in-situ gelled polymer electrolyte. The researchers also demonstrated 241 cycles under specified laboratory conditions of 500 mA/g and 1,000 mAh/g. This is a laboratory result, not a commercially validated automotive battery-pack rating.
Researchers at the Illinois Institute of Technology and Argonne National Laboratory reported another approach in a
paper. Their solid-state lithium-air architecture used a four-electron reaction to form lithium oxide (Li₂O), rather than the more conventional lithium-peroxide pathway. The battery completed at least 1,000 charge-discharge cycles at room temperature. Its theoretical energy-density potential was estimated at 1,200 Wh/kg, not measured as an achieved commercial-cell rating.
These results show progress beyond theoretical calculations, but different chemistries, operating environments and measurement boundaries make direct comparisons difficult. None establishes a production-ready passenger-car battery.
Three engineering roadblocks for passenger cars
1. Air management adds weight and complexity
A lithium-air battery needs oxygen while limiting exposure to moisture and carbon dioxide. These contaminants can trigger unwanted reactions that degrade the lithium anode, electrolyte and cathode. Moisture can react with metallic lithium, while carbon dioxide can form lithium carbonate (Li₂CO₃). Deposits inside the porous cathode can restrict oxygen transport and reduce usable capacity.
An automotive system would therefore need controlled air intake, filtration and humidity management, potentially alongside additional gas-handling equipment. These components add weight and volume while consuming energy. A
2023 study in the
Journal of Energy Storage
proposed mechanical balance-of-plant systems for lithium-air vehicles. It estimated that the supporting equipment would consume 5.4% of battery power in its proposed vehicle configuration. The figure is design-specific, but illustrates the additional energy demand of operating lithium-air cells in a vehicle.
2. Rechargeability and efficiency remain difficult
Lithium peroxide must be removed from the cathode during charging. Reversing the discharge reaction requires additional energy and can generate reactive oxygen species that attack the electrolyte and other cell components.
These side reactions contribute to capacity loss and limited cycle life. Lithium-metal anodes also face instability during repeated lithium deposition and removal. High initial energy density therefore does not guarantee reliable performance over hundreds or thousands of cycles.
Lower round-trip efficiency increases the energy required to deliver a given amount of usable electricity. Some losses appear as heat, increasing thermal-management demands, while air-handling equipment adds further parasitic consumption. Cooling requirements must also be considered alongside battery weight, volume, and vehicle efficiency.
3. Energy density does not guarantee vehicle performance
Specific energy measures how much energy a battery stores per unit of mass, while volumetric energy density measures how much it stores within a given space. Power density determines how quickly it can deliver that energy.
Passenger cars need all three. A battery with exceptional specific energy but poor power output or low volumetric density would not automatically suit a vehicle platform. It must also deliver sufficient power for acceleration, overtaking and sustained driving while fitting within the available battery enclosure.
Battery swapping would not resolve these limitations. Although swapping can rotate packs between vehicles and charging stations, it cannot reverse chemical decomposition, restore damaged electrolytes or remove irreversible deposits inside degraded electrodes.
Solid-state research is part of the lithium-air story
Lithium-air batteries are not simply rivals to solid-state batteries. Researchers are also investigating solid electrolytes within lithium-air architectures to protect the lithium anode and stabilise electrochemical reactions.
The Argonne and Illinois Tech research demonstrates one such approach, using a composite solid electrolyte based on lithium-containing nanoparticles embedded in a polymer matrix. This does not establish that a particular ceramic such as garnet LLZO is a universal prerequisite for lithium-air technology. Lithium-air batteries and conventional solid-state lithium-ion batteries also remain fundamentally different technologies.
CATL’s nearer-term development priorities remain sodium-ion and all-solid-state batteries. Lithium-air still needs substantial progress in durability, power output, air management, efficiency and complete-system packaging before its suitability for passenger cars can be established.
High-altitude long-endurance uncrewed aircraft are sometimes discussed as potential applications for high-specific-energy batteries. That possibility should not be confused with a confirmed CATL deployment programme.
For now, the 2,000 km claims describe a theoretical possibility, not an automotive capability CATL has demonstrated. Turning lithium-air’s exceptional electrochemical potential into a durable, rechargeable and practical vehicle battery remains the much harder task.

title: EGI Battery Opens Japan Technical Center to Advance Development and Commercialization of Next-Generation Battery Cells - Batteries News
content:
EGI Battery Opens Japan Technical Center to Advance Development and Commercialization of Next-Generation Battery Cells
Yokohama-based EGI Battery KK launches its Japan Technical Center to strengthen R&D, materials science, and supply-chain capabilities to support advanced lithium-ion battery development, manufacturing, supplier partnerships and customer relationships across Asia Pacific.
ANN ARBOR, Mich., Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — EGI Battery, a U.S.-owned lithium-ion battery cell company, today announces the establishment of EGI Battery KK, its Japanese subsidiary, and the official opening of its Japan Technical Center in Yokohama. Japan’s history of battery innovation, advanced manufacturing know-how and experienced talent make it a strategic location to bolster EGI’s technical operations.
EGI Battery KK’s Technical Center will initially focus on conducting research & development, evaluating advanced battery materials, and strengthening supplier relationships and technology partnerships to support EGI’s advanced battery cell development and commercialization efforts.
Tom McGuckin,
CEO of EGI Battery, said:
Building better batteries takes more than a breakthrough in the lab.
”It takes capabilities to connect materials, engineering and manufacturing to produce batteries which enable our customers’ technology. Establishing EGI Battery KK is a strategic investment in those capabilities. By connecting Japan’s deep battery expertise with the manufacturing operations we are building in Michigan, we aim to bring the next generation of advanced lithium-ion batteries into production and expand what our customers can achieve.”
EGI Battery KK also establishes a local base for working directly with customers and partners across Asia Pacific. The team will help connect regional market needs with EGI’s cell development and commercialization efforts. McGuckin added, “This regional presence deepens collaboration between our technical development activities and our customers’ applications.”
Junji Tabuchi, President of EGI Battery KK, will lead the Yokohama operation, including its technical partnerships and regional business development activities. Tabuchi brings more than 35 years of lithium-ion battery experience across UBE Corporation, NEC TOKIN and E-One Moli Energy, including leadership of battery materials R&D at UBE.
The opportunity is not only to develop better battery materials, but to turn those advances into cells that can be manufactured reliably and meet demanding customer requirements
“Our initial focus is on materials, R&D and our supplier partnerships. We are intentionally building a strong technical foundation in Japan so we can move promising research and engineering into commercial production.”
As the Japan operations develop, EGI Battery KK plans to expand into cell design, with a focus on electrodes, and then battery manufacturing capabilities. These future capabilities will leverage the center’s initial materials, supply-chain and R&D activities, strengthening EGI’s ability to develop and validate new battery technologies.
The Japan Technical Center complements EGI’s manufacturing expansion in Ann Arbor, Michigan. Through a phased approach, EGI is building the production capabilities and technical expertise needed to manufacture advanced lithium-ion pouch cells at scale. The Japan operation’s initial materials evaluation, R&D and supplier collaboration will support that work, strengthening the connection between battery innovation and U.S. production.

title: Graphite One Engages Ames National Laboratory to Assess Rare Earth Recoveries from Alaska's Graphite Creek Deposit - Batteries News
content:
Graphite One Engages Ames National Laboratory to Assess Rare Earth Recoveries from Alaska’s Graphite Creek Deposit
Three-month project with the Department of Energy Strategic Special Program will evaluate leaching, heavy and light rare earth separation, and a preliminary scalable process flowsheet
VANCOUVER, BC, Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Graphite One Inc. (TSXV: GPH) (OTCQX:
Graphite One,
” or the “
“) today announced a research program with Ames National Laboratory (“
Ames Lab
“) to assess and optimize a sustainable process for recovering rare earth elements (“
“) from garnet material from the Company’s Graphite Creek deposit near Nome, Alaska.
The work, conducted under a Strategic Partnership Project Agreement, will examine garnet preparation and characterization, acid leaching, separation of heavy rare earth elements (“
“) from light rare earth elements (“
“), and product purification. Funded by G1. the program is intended to develop a preliminary scalable flowsheet and evaluate its mass balance, reagent use, water consumption and waste generation. The three-month project will commence immediately.
Anthony Huston,
President and CEO of Graphite One, said:
Graphite Creek’s garnets host rare earth elements, including the heavy rare earths and magnet metals that are critical to U.S. technology and the Defense Industrial Base,
“Partnering with Ames National Laboratory, the Department of Energy’s premier rare earths research institution with more than 75 years of expertise, gives us a rigorous, independent path to assess their recovery potential. Our objective is clear: to determine how much additional value these rare earths can add to what is already the largest natural graphite deposit in the United States.”
Ames Lab G1 REE Work Plan
The Ames Lab program will begin with mineralogical and chemical characterization of the Graphite Creek garnet material, comminution and mechano-chemical activation, followed by preliminary acid-leaching tests. Subsequent work will optimize leaching conditions and screen separation approaches, including solvent extraction, stepwise pH adjustment and fractional crystallization. The final phase will assess precipitation and purification of REE group products and prepare an integrated flowsheet and mass balance.
Graphite Creek REE Potential
The Ames Lab program follows earlier work conducted in 2025 by Graphite One in which garnet grains were mechanically separated from crushed Graphite Creek drill-core samples at the University of Alaska Fairbanks and analyzed for REE concentrations by Activation Laboratories (“
ACTLabs found that 85% of the REEs in the tested garnet material were magnet or heavy rare earths. The analysis reported dysprosium concentrations of 32–63 ppm, yttrium of 198–427 ppm and scandium of 84–141 ppm. Graphite Creek garnets appeared to host much of the HREEs, scandium and yttrium; the separated garnet fraction showed two to six times higher REE concentrations than the remaining material.
Graphite One’s U.S. Supply Chain Strategy
Graphite One is advancing a vertically integrated domestic graphite strategy designed to reduce U.S. dependence on foreign-sourced graphite and establish an American supply chain extending from raw material through advanced materials manufacturing.
The Company’s strategy includes:
Mining and processing natural graphite at Graphite Creek, Alaska
Transporting graphite materials through the Port of Nome
Manufacturing advanced graphite and anode materials in Ohio
Potential co-located recycling of graphite and other battery materials
This integrated approach is designed to establish a domestic supply chain spanning resource development, advanced materials manufacturing and potential recycling – supporting the development of a circular U.S. graphite materials economy and continues to remain subject to project financing.

title: Korea sends trade chief to Hungary to support battery firms amid tightening regulations - Batteries News
content:
Korea sends trade chief to Hungary to support battery firms amid tightening regulations
The South Korean government has moved to address difficulties facing Korean companies in Hungary after the country’s new government tightened environmental regulations on battery manufacturing facilities.
The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy said Park Jeong-seong, chief of the ministry’s trade negotiation bureau, visited Hungary on Monday (local time) and held separate meetings with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Orban, Economy and Energy Minister Istvan Kapitany, and Regional Development Minister Viktoria Lorincz.
The visit came amid growing uncertainty over battery operations in Hungary following the tightening of environmental regulations after the new government of Prime Minister Magyar Peter took office in May.
Park told his counterparts that South Korea, as Hungary’s largest Asian investor, has contributed to the country’s economic development through job creation and supply chain strengthening in advanced manufacturing sectors including automobiles, batteries and electronics.
Park stressed the importance of the battery sector as a strategic industry for Hungary’s carbon neutrality and renewable energy goals, and as a driver of synergies with related industries such as electric vehicles, urging Hungarian officials to ensure Korean companies can operate smoothly in the country.
Park also argued that Korean companies actively leveraging the production base and technological capabilities they have built in Hungary aligns with the intent of the EU’s Industrial Acceleration Act, which favors locally produced goods, and would enhance Hungary’s standing as a key production and supply hub within Europe.
On the EU Battery Regulation — which mandates carbon emissions reporting, the use of recycled materials and supply chain due diligence — Park requested that Korean companies be given sufficient preparation time and that the regime be administered reasonably.
Park then co-hosted a joint ESG management declaration ceremony with Korean battery companies operating in Hungary, the Korea Battery Industry Association, the South Korean Embassy in Hungary and KOTRA, reaffirming their commitment to voluntary compliance in environmental, health and safety matters and to building a mutually beneficial ecosystem.
Companies such as Samsung SDI and SK On have invested more than $8 billion in Hungary, playing an important role in the economic and industrial development of both countries
“The government will actively support our companies so they can continue investing and operating in a stable environment while fulfilling their social responsibilities.”
Hungary emerged as a major European production hub for batteries under former Prime Minister Viktor Orban’s government, which focused heavily on attracting foreign direct investment to develop the sector. The policy direction shifted sharply after the new government took office and began tightening regulations.
Samsung SDI and SK On have both been fined for environmental regulation violations, adding to the mounting business risks the two companies face.

RAYMOND ADVANCES LITHIUM-ION BATTERY INNOVATION FROM MANUFACTURING TO LIFECYCLE MANAGEMENT
Raymond celebrates the assembly of its 2,500
lithium-ion battery and advances second-life and recycling solutions to support sustainability goals
GREENE, N.Y., Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — The Raymond Corporation is leading the way as it continues to transform and grow its battery and energy storage solutions reaching a significant milestone: the production of its 2,500
next-generation lithium-ion battery. This achievement reflects the company’s continued investment in advanced energy solutions designed to help material handling operations improve productivity, manage energy consumption, and meet the evolving demands of modern warehouse operations.
Matt Boecke,
general manager of energy solutions at The Raymond Corporation, said:
Lithium-ion technology is creating new opportunities for customers to get more from every shift,
“Through continued investment in manufacturing and energy innovation, Raymond is delivering solutions that drive customer value. Our lithium-ion batteries can deliver up to 17% greater productivity than lead-acid batteries, with thermal management for cold-storage applications and integrated monitoring capabilities that help optimize performance in demanding environments.”
As adoption of lithium-ion technology continues to grow, Raymond is committed to supporting its customers beyond battery deployment through recycling solutions that help extend value and reduce environmental impact. Raymond offers customers the second-life phase of its energy systems primarily through its lithium-ion take-back program and advanced grid integration research. The focus is on extending the lifecycle and maintaining a circular economy for its lithium-ion intralogistics batteries.
Raymond’s approach to lithium-ion technology considers the battery lifecycle alongside the equipment it powers. Advanced electrification, investments in energy solutions and advanced technologies are being introduced to support the industry’s mission to find ways to extend battery life; battery health assessments can help identify innovative opportunities for lithium-ion batteries remaining useful life. Raymond is also exploring opportunities to extend the useful life and value of lithium-ion batteries beyond their initial material handling applications, including potential energy-as-a-service solutions and future applications in battery energy storage systems.
Balki Iyer,
Founder & CEO of Bridge Green Upcycle, a NY-based battery upcycling company, said:
As electrification accelerates and the need for critical minerals increases, reliable battery recycling and advanced diagnostics are essential to building a more circular battery ecosystem
“Our partnership with Raymond strengthens our role as a trusted battery life cycle provider, both for our patented, AI-enabled Battery Health Monitoring Software and critical mineral recovery process. Being selected by an industry leader like Raymond is a validation for our commitment to the highest standards of safety and quality, as we work together to advance battery reuse, repurposing and recycling.”

title: RWE starts construction of its first battery in Italy - Batteries News
content:
RWE starts construction of its first battery in Italy
Essen/Rome, 10 November 2026
RWE has started construction of its first Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) in Italy.
The 62,5-megawatts (MW) Ragusa battery will be located in Sicily. It will consist of 42 containers with lithium-ion batteries, being able to deliver its maximum output for 4 hours. This corresponds to a nominal storage capacity of 262,5 megawatt hours (MWh). Commissioning is scheduled for the end of 2027.
Sopna Sury,
CEO RWE Renewables Europe & Australia, said:
The start of construction of our Ragusa battery storage marks an important milestone.
”We have been operating in Italy for many years, using the energy from the wind and the sun. In a world of growing renewable energy, battery storage systems are crucial for stabilising the grid and ensuring that electricity is used when it is needed most. Ragusa battery will be capable of covering the evening peak demand of around 21.000 households for 4 hours. We look forward to establishing further battery storage capacity in Italy soon – in addition to wind and solar power – in order to support Italy in building a resilient energy system.”
Ragusa battery will provide balancing energy to stabilise the electricity grid. It also features the technology necessary to provide new grid forming services such as instantaneous reserve (inertia). In addition to the batteries, RWE will build the associated grid infrastructure. This includes a high-voltage transformer to connect to the 150-kV grid.
Battery storage at RWE
As a driver of the energy transition, RWE develops, builds and operates
battery storage systems
in the US, Europe and Australia. Globally, RWE currently operates battery storage systems with a total capacity of around 1.7 gigawatts (GW) and 3 GW are under construction. As an integral part of its growth strategy, RWE plans to significantly expand its battery storage capacities worldwide.
RWE Renewables Italia – strong presence in Italy’s renewables market
RWE is a key player in the Italian renewables market. The company takes an integrated project approach that incorporates the development, construction and operation as well as the marketing of wind farms and solar plants. With 18 onshore wind farms, one photovoltaic plant and three agrivoltaic plants in operation, RWE currently manages a total installed capacity of approximately 670 MW in Italy, enough to supply green electricity to more than 550,000 Italian households. In addition, RWE currently has around 200 MW of further wind and solar capacity under construction in Italy.

Samsung SDI – AI data center backup battery wins CES 2027 Innovation Award
Samsung SDI’s space-saving UPS battery for AI data centers earned a 2027 CES Innovation Award for power, energy density and fire safety.
Samsung SDI’s prismatic battery solution for uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems won the 2027 CES Innovation Award for the world’s largest electronics trade show set to take place in Las Vegas in January.
The Korean battery maker said Tuesday its SDI U8A3-UPS, an uninterruptible power supply that provides emergency power to critical facilities like AI data centers during blackouts, won in the enterprise tech category.
The system was recognized for its very high power output, high energy density and fire safety, Samsung SDI said.
It uses prismatic cells made with lithium manganese oxide, which makes it 33 percent more space-efficient than conventional products, so fewer units are needed to deliver stable power.
It can also supply backup power during sudden surges in demand from AI computing, which helps prevent server failures and data loss.

title: Tesla plans to start battery cell production in Germany by mid-2027 - Batteries News
content:
Tesla plans to start battery cell production in Germany by mid-2027
The Grünheide gigafactory is set to add 4680 cells to its Model Y lineup, backed by nearly €1 billion and more than 1,500 planned hires
’s plant in Grünheide, just outside Berlin, is set to begin making its own battery cells in the middle of next year. The target is mid-2027, and the cell in question is Tesla’s 4680-format cylindrical design.
What Tesla is building in Grünheide
The plan calls for scaling cell output to as much as
per year. A gigawatt-hour measures how much energy a battery can store, so this is a measure of storage built, not electricity used.
To staff it, Tesla plans to hire more than
new employees for cell manufacturing.
The money is already moving. Cumulative investment in Grünheide’s battery cell production is approaching
€1 billion
The project will also use Tesla’s dry-electrode coating technology. Tesla’s bet is that this method makes battery manufacturing more efficient.
Tesla is not stopping at one building, either. The company aims to file for permits on a second large production hall in December 2026. That structure is expected to cover roughly 536,000 square meters.
Why make batteries in Europe at all
Producing in Germany is not the budget option. Manufacturing costs in the region run higher than in Asia, where much of the world’s battery supply chain is concentrated.
The move is also about supply chain resilience and the ability to iterate on production faster. In Grünheide, the plan is to build cells, packs, and finished cars all side by side, with the Model Y as the headline vehicle.
The bigger picture for Tesla’s European operations
Grünheide has served as Tesla’s main manufacturing foothold in Europe. Adding cell production turns it from an assembly hub into something closer to a full-stack factory.
The December 2026 permit filing for a second hall signals that Tesla is thinking beyond a single expansion phase.
What this means
The risks are real. Higher regional production costs mean the economics depend heavily on whether dry-electrode coating delivers the efficiency gains Tesla is counting on. A new process, a new workforce of more than 1,500 people, and a new product line all launching at once is a lot of moving parts.
Mid-2027 is the target, and an 18 GWh annual capacity is where Tesla intends to scale over time.
The milestones to track are straightforward. First, whether cell production actually starts on schedule in mid-2027. Second, how quickly output climbs toward the 18 GWh ceiling. Third, whether the December 2026 permit filing happens as planned and how regulators respond.

title: Why Greenpeace Interrupted Jensen Huang’s Keynote
content:
Nvidia and the wider tech sector are currently confronting the so-called key-man risk long associated with Jensen Huang, who
resigned as Nvidia’s CEO
on Thursday, Nov. 12.
That dynamic was on display at Nvidia GTC Berlin, where then-CEO Huang delivered his usual one-person show, moving from high-level vision to technical deep dives.
That changed midway through the presentation, when the keynote briefly became an unscripted Q&A session. At least two
Greenpeace protesters unfurled a banner
and projected a message onto the stage reading, “Clean Up Your Dirty Business.” They also shouted questions about Nvidia technology reportedly found in Russian drones, as well as the environmental effects of data center expansion.
Huang remained calm during the interruption and asked security not to overreact as the protesters were escorted from the hall.
“Everybody has a chance to say something,” Huang said. “I'll talk to you later. But let me get through my keynote.”
Related:
How Carbon-Aware Scheduling Can Cut Data Center Emissions
Greenpeace later said it was behind the protest and posted a statement on its website.
“While Nvidia is building an unchecked AI empire no one consented to, people are paying the price,” Benjamin Stephan, Big Tech campaigner at Greenpeace International, said in the
statement
. “Around the world, communities face damage to water supplies and soil, alongside rising electricity bills because of unchecked expansion of data centers.”
For its part, Nvidia says it is focused on sustainable growth. In the company’s
2026 Sustainability Report
, Huang wrote: “For the second consecutive year, Nvidia matched 100% of our global electricity consumption with clean energy. We continue to work to reduce emissions, improve efficiency across our operations, and design platforms like Vera Rubin so that powerful computing and sustainability advance together.”
Arguably, Nvidia has more immediate concerns at the moment than scrutiny and potential direct action tied to its sustainability efforts. But its data center operator customers are facing more pressure than ever on issues such as environmental impact and water use.
Why Nvidia Became a Protest Target
Data Center Knowledge
caught up with Greenpeace’s Stephan to learn more about the motivations behind the protest and whether further direct action targeting data centers and the wider tech sector is likely.
The interview has been edited for length and clarity.
Data Center Knowledge:
What happened in the immediate aftermath of the protest? I was sitting a couple of rows behind and saw the activists being escorted out by security. Did Huang deliver on his promise to speak to the protesters after his keynote?
Related:
Can Data Center Design Choices Change Public Acceptance?
Benjamin Stephan:
They didn't get arrested. They were taken outside, banned from re-entering the building, and then they left. I personally waited outside for Jensen Huang to talk to him when he came out.
Data Center Knowledge:
So you put yourself in a position to have that follow-up discussion, but it sounds like Jensen did not follow through?
Stephan:
Yes. I waited for him outside by his car and let his security detail know that he had said onstage that he wanted to talk afterward. But they did not enable this; instead, they had his car drive off empty.
Data Center Knowledge:
Were you a coordinator of that particular direct action? It must have been hard to smuggle the banner past what I thought was very tight security.
Stephan:
No. Because I am based in Berlin, I was there as a spokesperson and Big Tech campaigner for Greenpeace International, seeking a direct conversation with Huang. This action was part of Greenpeace’s sustained effort to hold Nvidia accountable, involving several Greenpeace organizations.
Previous actions included a
five-layered cake
topped with wind turbines that Greenpeace East Asia activists gave to Huang in Taipei. They used his metaphor [that
AI is a five-layered cake
] to illustrate the point that AI, in general, and Nvidia, in particular, are missing renewable energy. Confronted with the question, “Can you invest in renewable energy together with your suppliers in Taiwan?” Huang replied positively. We were in Berlin to hold him accountable, because nothing had happened yet.
Related:
Do Data Centers Really Drive Up Local Temperatures?
At Nvidia’s GTC Taipei conference, Greenpeace East Asia activists confronted Jensen Huang, calling on Nvidia to take responsibility for the growing energy demands and carbon emissions throughout its supply chain. (Image Credit: Greenpeace / Chong Kok Yew)
Data Center Knowledge:
What were you hoping to achieve at the GTC Berlin protest and in other actions at Nvidia events?
Stephan:
The goal was simple: let the public know and remind Jensen Huang that Nvidia needs to clean up its dirty business. That was the message on the banner and in the projection.
Security cut the activists short when they started elaborating, but the criticism is twofold.
First, Nvidia’s chips have
reportedly been found
in autonomous Russian drones deployed in Ukraine. That is unacceptable. The company needs to implement independent auditing across all global distributors, subsidiaries, and third-party vendors to guarantee that no Nvidia technology is used in ways that violate human rights or is diverted into military equipment or autonomous weapons.
Second, Nvidia’s supply chain largely runs on fossil fuels, exacerbating the climate crisis. This also creates significant hardship for communities in Taiwan, where Nvidia relies on
to manufacture its chips. All of this is happening even though it would only take a fraction of Nvidia’s gigantic profits to switch its supply chain to renewables.
To make things worse, Nvidia is now involved in organizing financing models to make it easier for its Big Tech customers to finance new data centers and buy its chips, further fueling the unchecked expansion of data centers. More often than not, these data centers also rely on fossil fuels, making Nvidia’s carbon footprint even worse.
Nvidia needs to commit to 100% renewable energy across its supply chain and data center investments by 2030 and stop relying on fossil and
nuclear power
. It also needs to invest in new renewable capacity worldwide, especially in key supplier regions like Taiwan and in places where Nvidia is investing heavily, such as Southeast Asia.
What Greenpeace Plans Next for the Data Center Sector
Data Center Knowledge:
We have seen significant
pushback against data centers
Stephan:
Peaceful protest and nonviolent direct action are part of Greenpeace’s DNA. They are also part of Greenpeace’s new global campaign on Big Tech. Only a few days after the protest at GTC, Greenpeace activists joined the Stop Dirty Data Centres coalition for two days of action, with local protests in Europe and around the world.

title: Ampeak completes battery installation at 240 MWh Uskmouth project - Energy Storage
content: Scotland-headquartered developer and operator Ampeak Energy has completed the delivery and installation of all battery units and major equipment for the first phase of its 120 MW / 240 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) at the Uskmouth Sustainable Energy Park in Newport, South Wales. This marks a key construction milestone, with energization planned later this month. The Afon Wysg 1 (AW1) project is scheduled to enter commercial operation in Q1 2027. Ampeak is also progressing plans to expand the site to 480 MWh, with financial close for the second phase targeted shortly after the initial project becomes operational. Ampeak said that Canadian Solar subsidiary e-Storage supplied 55 battery units for AW1 and will be responsible for commissioning. Jones Bros Civil Engineering UK completed installation of the batteries, along with 36 inverters, 18 twin skids, and the project’s main grid transformer. The project was given a Notice of Decision by the Newport City Council on 8th May 2025, and initial phases of the project, including a submitted “Battery Management Plan: Afon Wysg Battery Energy Storage System by Enso Energy” was first submitted in July 2023. Enso Energy sold the project to the then SAE Renewables which rebranded as Ampeak in August 2025. Now, construction works have also been completed, including concrete foundations, installation of power conversion system infrastructure and construction of a new on-site substation. Ampeak said about two-thirds of the existing power station export cable and also listed other measures to reduce overall environmental impacts, including reusing materials such as crushed concrete and an attenuation pond set up to reduce run-off. The developer said the site has been designed to accommodate future expansion, with foundations already poured and space left between the batteries for the second phase. “We’re thrilled to see the project continuing its excellent progress and look forward to reaching our next major milestone, which will be the first energization of the batteries from the grid later this month, which will be followed by the charge and discharge commissioning, all ensuring that we reach our target for energization this month and full commercial operation in Q1 2027,” said Ampeak’s CEO Designate, David Taaffe. “We will then move to rapidly financially close the expansion to 480 MWh which can be implemented with minimal disruption to the 240 MWh operating asset.” More: Canadian Solar’s e-Storage aims to supply around 1 GW of BESS capacity for Brazil’s first capacity reserve auction , scheduled for December 2 The post Ampeak completes battery installation at 240 MWh Uskmouth project appeared first on Energy Storage .

title: Australian developer seeks suppliers for 450 MW BESS and solar project - Energy Storage
content: Renewables developer Central Queensland Power (CQP) has launched an expressions of interest (EOI) process seeking suppliers for the proposed Wooderson solar and battery energy storage project being developed near the Queensland industrial hub of Gladstone. The project , planned for a site at Mount Alma, approximately 40 km southwest of Gladstone, includes a 450 MW solar facility along with a 450 MW DC-coupled battery energy storage system (BESS) with up to 3,600 MWh of storage. CQP, a joint venture between Sydney-based Energy Estate and the Australian arm of United Kingdom-headquartered clean energy company RES, has now opened an EOI through Gateway by ICN. Anticipated supply chain requirements span civil and electrical balance of plant works, equipment supply, high-voltage infrastructure, transport, logistics, commissioning and skilled labour. The developer is aiming to secure the supply of about 980,000 solar panels, a 450 MW BESS, substation, switching yard, 275 kV transmission connection, electrical infrastructure, access roads and construction facilities. Procurement for lead construction contractors is expected to progress later this year with construction currently targeted for the first quarter of 2028, with completion expected by December 2030, subject to approvals, financing and investment decisions. Small works procurement is expected to begin approximately six to nine months before construction. CQP estimates the Wooderson project will generate up to 680 jobs during the construction phase, and, once operational, would deliver about 1,300 GWh of renewable energy into the National Electricity Market a year. The project recently secured the first of three required planning approvals, covering a section of the proposed overhead transmission line within the Callide Infrastructure Corridor State Development Area (CICSDA). The project also holds an earlier environmental clearance from the Australian government, which determined it was not a controlled action under the EPBC Act. The project needs to also go through the Queensland government State Assessment and Referral Agency (SARA) for the solar farm and ancillary infrastructure including the BESS, and the Gladstone Regional Council for sections of the proposed overhead transmission line and switchyard located outside the CICSDA. title: Cyprus: Batteries installed in summer still await grid connection - Energy Storage
content: Limassol-headquartered CYPV Solar Holdings LTD installed six batteries at six of its solar parks in July . Of these energy storage systems, only one is operational, while the remaining five batteries are still awaiting grid connection terms from the local network operator . The six installed batteries have a combined capacity of 24 MW AC/55.6 MWh, and they were installed along six photovoltaic parks totaling 24 MW, a spokesperson for CYPV Solar Holdings told ESS News . Of these hybrid projects, only one is fully operational since July . Also remarkable is that the documentation of all applications for the grid connection of the six batteries filed in 2025 was identical . There is no difference between the kind of information and documents submitted for the five projects still waiting in the queue and that of the battery project that received grid connection terms, said the CYPV Solar Holdings spokesman . The company has lodged appeals with the network operator but hasn’t received a response yet . The sole operational project comprises 1 MW of a solar system and 1 MW/5.6 MWh of a battery . Moreover, all six batteries are installed in front of the meter . “The batteries are co-located (hybrid) storage installed in front of the meter. Each battery is AC-coupled to its PV park and shares the park’s single grid connection point and export limit. There is no on-site consumption load. The battery stores the park’s own output and exports it later through the same connection. It does not add export capacity beyond the PV rating,” said CYPV Solar Holdings . Apart from CYPV Solar Holdings’s 5.6 MWh operational battery system, Cyprus had also installed a separate utility battery in the summer through the Pavlina Memorial Energy Park , a hybrid facility combining 1.8 MW of photovoltaic generation with a 5 MWh battery . Electricity supplier Petrolina Electric, who is the investor behind the ‘Pavlina Memorial Energy Park’, claimed this was Cyprus’ first utility battery system that participated in the country’s electricity market . Cyprus has so far installed a bit over 1 GW of solar PV capacity but faces an acute green energy curtailment problem . In the first five months of 2026, Cyprus curtailed over 65% of potential solar generation and the country desperately needs energy storage systems . However, the case concerning CYPV Solar Holdings’s installed batteries that await grid connection since July shows Cyprus is unable to provide timely solutions . title: Elements Green receives grid connection commitment from TenneT for 1.6 GWh BESS in Germany - Energy Storage
content: Another large-scale energy storage project is taking shape: Elements Green’s German subsidiary has signed a grid connection agreement with transmission system operator TenneT for a battery storage facility in Stadorf near Uelzen. The facility will have a capacity of 400 MW and a storage capacity of 1.6 GWh. It will be directly connected to the high-voltage grid. Following the signing of the connection construction contract at the beginning of this year, the grid connection contract represents another important step toward realizing the project. The next steps include detailed planning of the grid connection infrastructure and preparation for construction. Elements Green signed a deal with Envision Energy , likely for its Gen-8 battery energy storage system, for the supply of the BESS back at Intersolar 2026 in Munich. Two billion euros investment planned The London-based company is developing several more large-scale battery storage systems in Germany, intended to connect to the high-voltage grid. Elements Green is responsible for financing, developing, and operating the storage facilities. Just over a year ago, Elements Green announced its intention to connect eight battery storage systems with a combined capacity of 3.2 GW to the grid in Germany by 2027. This includes a 400 MW storage system with a four-hour storage duration in Alfstedt near Bremerhaven. At the time, the company said it planned to invest a total of two billion euros in Germany by the end of 2028. “Germany needs not only additional renewable generation capacity but, above all, the high-performance and flexible infrastructure to make the energy transition a technical and economic success. Large-scale battery storage systems such as Stadorf will play a central role in this,” Zimmermann added. title: Flower plans 2 GWh BESS in Germany, near Berlin - Energy Storage
content: Flower plans to build a 500 MW/2,000 MWh battery storage system at the Ragow substation in Lübbenau, some 100 kilometers south-east of Berlin, and near a popular tourist destination. The Swedish company acquired the project last year and is currently developing it with DCES, it announced Monday. DCES leads project development, while Flower is to handle financing, technical planning, procurement, construction and, later, operation and marketing. Building permit applications have been submitted. Flower expects the project in Brandenburg’s Spreewald region to reach ready-to-build status this year, with commercial operation scheduled for 2029. DCES has been developing projects in Germany for twelve years and holds a nationwide pipeline of 3,000 MW. The company said it will handle planning and development of the large-scale storage systems, as well as coordination with local stakeholders. Flower has only been active in the German market since last year, but it is expanding its pipeline rapidly. This year, it acquired a 112 MW battery storage portfolio from Chint Solar , plus a further 63 MW/257 MWh project in Saxony-Anhalt. It is also building self-developed projects, including a 100 MW/400 MWh system in Hamburg-Bergedorf. Beyond acquisitions, Flower has signed a virtual flexibility purchase agreement (FPA) with Engie in Germany. The virtual tolling deal secures financing for battery storage systems totaling 126 MW . Next year, Flower also plans to launch its in-house asset optimization algorithm on the German market, enabling coordinated control of energy assets. title: Tesla on Autopilot/FSD hit an overturned truck at 71 mph, killing 3
content:
A Tesla Model 3 drove into an overturned box truck on I-75 near Naples, Florida, killing two of its passengers and a man who had stopped to help. Tesla’s own report to federal regulators says Autopilot or “Full Self-Driving” was engaged, at 71 mph.
Police and local media covered the May 31 crash as a truck wreck in the dark, and none of it mentioned a driver-assist system. It’s the latest case in our ongoing investigation into fatal crashes hidden in Tesla’s NHTSA data, and it lands as Tesla’s monthly crash count hits another record.
What happened on I-75
Just before 4 a.m. on Sunday, May 31, 2026, the 31-year-old driver of a 2014 Freightliner lost the road near the Pine Ridge Road exit in Collier County, steered back onto southbound I-75, and flipped it, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The overturned truck ended up blocking the center and outside lanes.
Jonathan Garcia Arias, a 25-year-old Naples man and former Marine, was driving by in a BMW. He pulled over and got out to help the truck driver.
Then a southbound 2023 Tesla with five young men from Naples inside came up on the scene. FHP’s report says the front of the Tesla hit the underside of the overturned truck and Garcia Arias. Two of the Tesla’s passengers, aged 18 and 19, died at the scene, and Garcia Arias died later in the hospital. The 20-year-old driver and two more passengers were seriously hurt.
A few days later, FHP used the crash as a warning about stopping near wrecks on the interstate. Senior Trooper Kenn Watson said the Tesla driver would have seen only the truck’s underside, with “no lights, no reflectors, nothing warning them.”
So that’s the official story. A dark obstacle, a driver who couldn’t see it in time. Nobody said a word about Autopilot.
What Tesla told the federal government
Under NHTSA’s Standing General Order, automakers have to report crashes where a Level 2 driver-assist system was engaged within 30 seconds of impact and someone was killed or hurt. Tesla filed one for this crash.
It identifies the car as a 2023 Model 3 on a highway, flags a traffic incident on the roadway, and marks the automation “Engagement Status” as “Verified Engaged.” That means Tesla confirmed through its own telematics that Autopilot or FSD was on. It logs a pre-crash speed of 71 mph and a fatality, lists the Florida Highway Patrol as the investigating agency, and says it learned of the crash from police and the media.
Then it blacks out the crash narrative, the software version, and whether the road was within the system’s approved operating domain, all as “confidential business information.” That’s the same redaction Tesla applies to 99.9% of its reports.
The report also surfaced late. Tesla filed it as a 5-Day report, the urgent category for fatal crashes, but it didn’t land until Tesla’s September filings, more than three months after the crash. And Tesla lists law enforcement as one of the ways it found out about it.
How we matched it: Tesla logged the incident time as 07:56 UTC, which converts to 3:56 a.m. in Florida, two minutes off the 3:54 a.m. in FHP’s report. The city, the highway, the 2023 model year, the month and the fatal outcome all line up, and it’s the only fatal Tesla driver-assist report in Naples that month. It’s the same crash.
Tesla has been here before
A Tesla on driver-assist going highway speed into the underside of a big truck, in the dark, in Florida. If that sounds familiar, it should.
In 2016, Joshua Brown was killed near Williston when his Model S on Autopilot drove under a tractor-trailer crossing the highway. In 2019, Jeremy Banner died in Delray Beach when his Model 3 on Autopilot went under a trailer at 68 mph and had its roof sheared off. In both crashes, neither the driver nor the system braked.
Trooper Watson’s point was that a human couldn’t see the truck. But a big, unlit obstacle sitting across two lanes at night is exactly the kind of thing a driver-assist system is supposed to catch, and Tesla now sells FSD as nearly ready to drive with nobody watching. And an attentive driver could clearly see it, as the BMW driver did, and stop before the Tesla arrived.
We want to be fair about what the data doesn’t prove. “Engaged within 30 seconds” is the reporting trigger. Tesla’s 71 mph may be a telematics snapshot rather than the impact speed. And with the software version redacted, we can’t say whether this was Autopilot or FSD.
A new record: 264 crashes in September
The NHTSA release that surfaced this crash, covering filings through October 15, also set a new monthly high. Tesla reported 264 driver-assist crashes in September 2026, beating July’s 236, which was itself a record. That’s up from 135 in March.
September may still grow as late reports come in. This Naples crash shows how late they can be.
Our merged dataset now holds 4,669 Tesla driver-assist crash reports since 2019, 69 of them flagged fatal. The same release added two other fatal reports, both “Verified Engaged” and both covered locally with no mention of driver-assist: a Model Y that hit a tree and burned in El Dorado Hills, California, killing three, and a Model X that hit a signal pole in Naples on September 30, killing a passenger. We’ll lay those out separately.
Electrek’s Take
Three people died on I-75, including a man who got out of his car to help a stranger. Tesla knows its driver-assist was on, knows the speed, holds the telematics, and filed a federal report saying so. Then it sealed everything that would explain what the car did, and the public got a story about a dark truck.
Top comment by Aigars Mahinovs
That's what happens when the system has to identify all objects in the camera frame before it can start to estimate the objects position and then relative distance and then relative velocity. Unrecognizable objects will destroy all your logic. This is a design failure and not something Tesla can actually fix.
Compare that to radars and lidars that directly measure distances and relative velocities of everything in front of the car, regardless of what it is. That is a far better approach because you do not want the car the impact objects on its trajectory regardless of what those objects turn out to be.
Tesla’s whole pitch for FSD is that the car sees better than you do, and yet, Tesla vehicles on Autopilot and FSD keep crashing on stationary objects on the highway. It’s the same failure that killed Joshua Brown and Jeremy Banner years ago. If the system saw the truck and the driver overrode it, Tesla should say so. It was quick to do that in the Katy crash when the data helped it. If the system didn’t see it, that’s a safety defect regulators and owners need to know about.
Either way, the redaction protects Tesla, not the people on the road. It’s the same pattern we found in Vineland and in July’s four fatal crashes, and the crash count keeps setting records.
We’re asking the Florida Highway Patrol for the full crash report, whether its investigators got Tesla’s raw vehicle data, and whether they even knew the system was engaged. If they didn’t, the only party that knows what this car did is the one that sealed the file.

title: Volkswagen prices its new ID. Cross for the UK, but the $35,000 version comes later
content:
Volkswagen
Peter Johnson
| Nov 16 2026 - 7:02 am PT
Volkswagen
revealed how much its new ID. Cross will cost, with prices starting at around $35,000 in the UK. But if you’re hoping to get the cheaper version, you’ll have to wait a bit longer.
Volkswagen ID. Cross prices by trim in the UK
After opening orders for the ID. Cross in Europe in July, Volkswagen is preparing to launch the entry-level electric SUV in the UK.
The ID. Cross is the all-electric equivalent of the T-Cross, Volkswagen’s smallest and most affordable SUV in Europe and the UK.
Following
the ID. Polo
, the ID. Cross is the latest from Volkswagen’s electric urban family of compact cars.
The electric SUV is 4,153 mm long, about the same length as the T-Cross, but its dedicated MEB+ platform offers more interior space. It seats five and offers a 475-liter boot, 20 liters more than the gas-powered T-Cross with the rear seats pushed all the way forward.
When the rear seats are folded, the electric ID. Cross offers up to 1,345 liters of overall luggage volume.
Like in Europe, the Volkswagen ID. Cross will be available with two battery packs in the UK: a 37 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) pack and a 52 kWh nickel-manganese-cobalt (NMC) pack.
The ID. Cross with the larger 52 kWh battery offers up to 265 miles of WLTP range, while the 37 kWh version provides up to 194 miles of WLTP range.
With DC fast charging of up to 105 and 88 kW, Volkswagen said the vehicle’s battery can charge from 10% to 80% in as little as 23 minutes.
All versions are equipped with vehicle-to-load (V2L) capabilities, allowing it to be used as a mobile power bank for an e-bike, campsite, or other external electronic devices.
Inside, the ID. Cross adopts VW’s revamped interior digital cockpit design. Cross adopts VW’s revamped interior digital cockpit design. The setup includes a 10.25″ Digital Cockpit Pro instrument display and a 12.9″ infotainment screen. Based on driver feedback, Volkswagen brought back physical buttons for climate control and other vehicle functions.
Volkswagen will open orders for the ID. Cross Life and Style trims in
with the 52 kWh battery and 208 hp (211 PS) motor will go on sale on Thursday, November 19, starting at £30,260 ($40,000) and £33,675 ($44,500), respectively.
The base ID. Cross Life and Style trims with the 37 kWh battery will go on sale in January 2027, with prices starting at £26,985 ($35,500) and £30,400 ($40,100).
Volkswagen said the 52 kWh version is eligible for the UK government’s £1,500 ($2,000) electric car grant. Eligibility for the 37 kWh versions is expected to be confirmed soon.

title: TCL中环组件业务销量增长，上调关联销售额度至36亿元
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，11月13日，TCL中环发布公告，拟增加2026年度日常关联销售交易预计额度3亿元。调整后，公司向关联方销售产品及提供劳务的年度预计金额由33亿元提升至36亿元，主要涉及组件销售及服务费等业务。
根据公告，此次关联交易涉及惠州TCL光伏科技及其子公司宁波碳达光伏新能源科技有限公司、TCL Energy Solution Co.,Limited等关联方。2026年1-10月，TCL中环与上述关联方实际发生的销售交易金额为25.2亿元，较2025年全年销售金额有所增长。
对于此次增加关联交易额度的原因，TCL中环表示，主要基于公司组件业务销量及市场份额增长，以满足业务实际发展需要和持续经营需求。相关交易将按照市场价格或双方参照市场协议价格执行。
光伏业务方面，TCL中环在11月15日披露的投资者关系活动记录表中表示，公司将继续坚持适度一体化和全球化战略，推动组件出货增长及海外收入占比提升。其中，硅片业务将重点优化客户结构、提高高端产品占比；组件业务则将拓展地方能源及分布式市场，优化产品和客户结构，提高高端化、差异化产品及订单占比。
公司计划于2026年至2027年分阶段完成20GW BC产线技改。衢州工厂约6GW产线已完成改造并进入量产爬坡阶段，预计年内BC组件出货约2GW。忻州工厂自9月启动技改，部分设备已到场调试。公司预计2027年上半年完成20GW产线调试和爬坡，力争于2027年年中在效率、成本和生产运营方面达到行业领先水平。

title: “十五五”新型储能目标：到2030年全国装机3亿千瓦
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，11月13日下午，国家发改委、国家能源局正式印发《“十五五”新型储能实施方案》，明确新型储能发展主线。新型储能从规模化发展迈入市场化发展新阶段，告别简单强制配储，转向以系统需求定规模、以价值变现为核心。
根据方案内容，清晰地锚定阶段性发展目标。
其中，到2030年，全国新型储能装机3亿千瓦，平均时长3小时左右；
定位来看，新型储能将重点承担源网荷侧日内调节，服务新能源消纳、顶峰保供、电网安全稳定；
从细分规模指引来看，省内自用储能超2.4亿千瓦；基地配套储能5000–6000万千瓦；电网侧可承担顶峰保供独立储能约1.4亿千瓦；
产业目标来看，产业链自主可控，保持全球竞争力，完善市场机制，兑现储能可靠容量价值。
本次方案最大变化是配储逻辑从“项目强制配套”转向“系统需求导向”，电网侧独立储能的顶峰保供价值被放到更高位置，市场化机制建设成为“十五五”储能的核心抓手。
此外，围绕上述目标，方案部署以下重点方向：
1.首先是科学布局，按需配储不再一刀切摊派风光配储指标，优先向有顶峰保供、消纳刚需、系统安全短板区域布局，区分省内自用、基地配套、跨省外送配套三类储能。
2.多元场景落地做强源侧配套、电网侧独立储能、用户侧储能；重点发展虚拟电厂、零碳园区、绿电直连、配网储能、应急保供、新能源非电利用等创新场景。
3.方案提出多条技术路线并行推进，巩固锂电优势，规模化推广钠离子电池；推动液流、压缩空气等长时储能商业化；飞轮、重力、熔盐储热试点；布局固态电池、氢储能等前沿技术攻关，完善构网型储能示范。
4.技术落地之后，打通市场化价值变现通道支持储能公平参与电能量、辅助服务市场；健全容量价值机制，完善充放电价格、系统成本分摊机制，解决储能收益单一、价值难以体现的痛点。
5.市场机制有序运行，需要配套规则与安全底线保驾护航。调度、安全与行业规范升级统一并网调度规则，强化全过程安全管控，压实项目主体责任；完善标准体系，依托全国新型储能大数据平台开展监测与后评价。
6.长远来看，产业的健康成长同样关键。引导产业链良性发展防范低端产能过剩，推动材料、系统集成、回收利用全链条提质；鼓励技术迭代，稳妥开展国际合作。

title: 亿纬锂能等4企储能订单与合作落地
content:
近期，特隆美储能、沃太能源、国瑞协创接连推进海外储能订单及合作，新宙邦与亿纬锂能签署60万吨电解液长期供货协议。
特隆美储能签署尼日利亚储能订单
11月13日，特隆美储能与尼日利亚光伏及储能企业Asolar、肯尼亚电力解决方案企业Munja先后签署首轮储能产品采购合同及三方战略合作框架。
根据首轮采购合同，Asolar向特隆美储能采购Ymir 5K及配套PCS、EMS等设备，用于尼日利亚某农场的离网光伏储能项目。
在第二轮三方合作框架中，三方锁定了首轮交付后的第二阶段追加采购，将重点开发尼日利亚金矿等项目。后续三方还将围绕尼日利亚、肯尼亚等非洲市场，推进工商业储能产品供应、光储柴微电网及储能产品本地化组装等业务。
新宙邦与亿纬锂能签60万吨电解液供应协议
11月13日，深圳新宙邦科技股份有限公司发布公告称，近日与惠州亿纬锂能股份有限公司签订《长期供货协议》，有效期自双方盖章之日起至2030年12月31日止。
根据协议，新宙邦承诺在2026年至2030年期间，向亿纬锂能供应预计需求量为60万吨的电解液产品，实际订单数量可在预计需求量基础上上下浮动10%（含10%）。其中，2029年及2030年的预测采购量属于意向性指标，不构成强制性履约承诺，具体产品名称、规格型号、单价及数量以双方书面确认的订单为准。
此外，为保障原材料稳定供应及产能锁定，亿纬锂能同意在协议生效后30个工作日内向新宙邦支付一定金额预付款，专项用于向上游供应商锁定核心原材料产能。
沃太能源签署缅甸30MWh离网光储项目订单
11月11日，沃太能源集团股份有限公司与缅甸独家代理商SANDISOLAR正式签署丹老30MWh离网光储一体化项目协议。
该项目位于缅甸丹老离网海岛高密度虾类养殖区。根据协议，沃太能源将为该基地打造“光储柴”协同供电方案，其中储能系统承担调峰、电力支撑及应急备电功能，在柴油发电机检修或故障时维持供电，以保障增氧、水循环及智能投喂等设备全天候连续运行，降低柴油消耗。
项目执行方面，沃太能源将提供储能系统解决方案及全周期交付支持，SANDISOLAR则依托其本地资源与服务网络推进项目落地。
国瑞协创与印度企业签署5GWh储能合作
11月11日，贝特瑞旗下储能子公司国瑞协创与印度Pai Kane集团旗下Pai Kane Energy在深圳签署战略合作备忘录。双方将围绕印度工商业及公用事业储能市场展开合作，目标到2030年累计合作规模达到5GWh。
目前，双方合作的首批6台GR261L储能柜已完成出厂测试、海运及印度清关程序，正式运抵客户现场，该批设备采用Pai Kane Energy品牌交付。
根据分工，国瑞协创将负责产品技术、工程设计及系统集成；Pai Kane Energy则依托当地EPC与渠道网络，牵头印度本地的产品开发、销售、项目交付及售后服务。随着后续交付规模扩大，双方计划分阶段推进本地化生产，先在印度开展本地组装，再探讨共同投资建厂。

title: 采用半固态电池！上海60MW/240MWh独立储能电站开工
content:
11月11日，上海怡云60MW/240MWh电网侧独立储能电站项目开工奠基仪式在上海市奉贤区综合保税区举行，项目总投资2.7亿元。
项目位于上海市奉贤区综合保税区，占地面积约26.5亩。采用35MW/140MWh磷酸铁锂电池储能系统与25MW/100MWh新型半固态电池储能系统协同配置，新建一座110kV升压站，以1回110kV线路接入110kV普天泾站。
在产业带动方面，项目配套新能源产业投资约3000万元，达产后首年产值可达1.2亿元，是奉贤抢占新型储能“黄金赛道”的关键项目。项目不仅是城市重要能源基础设施，更将成为区域产业跃升的绿色引擎，以储能电站建设为支点，形成“服务电网、反哺产业、集聚产业、升级产业”的综合效应。

German developer Hy2gen has finalised a €139.8m ($154m) European Hydrogen Bank (EHB) subsidy agreement for its planned 100MW Albatros green hydrogen project in Kassø. Denmark.
Awarded in the EHB’s third round, the deal lines the firm up for €0.97/kg ($1.07) for its first 10 years of operation, which is scheduled to begin in 2031.
With a final investment decision (FID) targeted in 2028, Hy2gen said the binding contract improves the 14,400 tonnes per year project’s “commercial foundation,” and could streamline progress toward financial close.
Under the EHB’s terms and conditions, it will need to reach this within two and a half years of signing the agreement and begin production within five.
Albatros is planned to supply German end-users via the Danish Hydrogen Backbone, joining three projects which were recently
awarded a combined
€1.2bn ($1.32bn) in subsidies under the associated, but separate, Germany-backed Auctions as a Service initiative.
Hy2Gen’s solidified deal is the second confirmed under the auction’s third round, with Norway’s Gen2 Energy
inking a deal
for €62m ($69m) last week.
Across the nine selected projects, over €1bn ($1.1bn) in subsidies are expected to be confirmed, funded by revenues raised from Europe’s emissions trading scheme.
Projects yet to sign agreements include MorGen Energy’s 300MW development in Denmark, Lotse PtX’s 120MW e-fuels facility in Germany, and Vetyalfa’s 500MW Cloudberry project in Vaaka, Finland.
While the majority were awarded subsidies between €0.44/kg ($0.48) and €1.10/kg ($1.21), the two maritime-centred winners, Gen2 and GreenH, landed subsidies close to €3.50/kg ($3.86).

title: AI Finds 28 Zero-Day Flaws In Physical Robotics Software
content:
This article is brought to you by VicOne.
VicOne identified an initial set of 28 zero-day findings in less than two days using AI-assisted research across software and tools supporting the Physical AI ecosystem. These include projects developed or maintained by Google, NVIDIA, and Meta, among others.
Based on initial validation, all 28 findings are classified as zero-day vulnerabilities. The count may change following vendor and vulnerability-authority review, and some findings do not yet have CVE tracking numbers.
Many of these tools help teams train, simulate, test, and operate robots. Weaknesses in them could influence the models teams build, the test results they trust, and the instructions sent to robots.
These findings create two demands for robotics teams: responding as AI helps uncover weaknesses faster, and assessing how each one could affect robot safety and operations.
What AI changes about vulnerability discovery
Vulnerability discovery involves examining code, tracing how systems communicate, and testing whether a suspected weakness can actually be exploited. AI can accelerate parts of this work, helping researchers analyze more software in less time. Attackers could use similar capabilities.
When the weakness is a zero-day — previously unknown and without an available fix — faster discovery can leave teams with little time to respond. While that exposure does not necessarily mean an attack has occurred, teams still need to determine whether they use the affected software and what an attacker could access or change.
Where the findings sit across the robot lifecycle
VicOne’s findings span three stages of the robotics lifecycle: development and training, simulation and validation, and deployment and runtime. Weaknesses at each stage could affect what a robot learns, how it is tested, and how it is controlled.
Figure 1. In this research set, 75% of findings involved development, training, simulation, or validation tools, highlighting risks that can arise before a robot is deployed.VicOne
The following scenarios show how a compromised component could influence the robot at each stage.
- Development and training: Hidden changes can reach the finished robot
A team downloads a pretrained model to adapt for its robot. Loading a malicious file could give an attacker access to the training system, allowing changes to training data or the model itself. A manipulated model could behave normally during routine testing but respond incorrectly to a particular object, scene, or command after deployment. The risk can enter through a tool the team trusts, before anyone attacks the robot directly.
- Simulation and validation: A passing test could give false confidence
Importing a compromised scene or robot model could give an attacker access to the simulation environment. With sufficient control, the attacker could alter simulated sensor readings, physical conditions, or test results. A robot could then appear to pass tests that should have exposed unsafe behavior, leading the team to approve it for real-world use on the basis of misleading evidence.
- Deployment and runtime: Operators could lose visibility or control
An attacker could exploit weaknesses to change files that influence motion planning or send malicious map data that crashes the operator’s monitoring display. Compromising a remote-operation computer could also put the instructions sent to the robot at risk. Depending on the system and its safeguards, these weaknesses could alter robot movement or leave operators unable to see what is happening and respond promptly.
These are potential consequences and not demonstrated outcomes for every finding. Actual effects depend on the attacker’s access, the system’s design, and whether other safeguards prevent the changes from reaching physical behavior.
In a separate demonstration, VicOne researchers provide a concrete example of a weakness affecting a protective function. The researchers exploited a vulnerability to prevent a robot’s remote-stop command from working. The case shows why teams need to test whether safeguards remain effective when the software supporting them is compromised.
Video 1. VicOne researchers demonstrate a vulnerability that prevents a robot’s remote-stop command from working. VicOne
A published patch still needs to be proven safe
AI can shorten the search for weaknesses, but a robotics team still needs to determine whether a fix is safe to deploy. Even after a software maintainer releases a patch, teams must identify affected systems, check compatibility, and verify that the update preserves intended behavior.
An earlier successful test remains useful evidence. However, a newly discovered weakness may reveal conditions that test never examined.
Three questions can help teams respond:
- Where do we use the affected software? Include training computers, simulation environments, and deployed robots.
- What could the weakness change? Assess whether it could affect models, test results, operator visibility, or robot behavior.
- How do we verify protection? Confirm that the fix addresses the weakness and that the updated system still operates as intended.
When immediate updating is impractical, teams may need temporary safeguards, such as restricting access to an affected service, while a validated fix is prepared.
As details from the 28 findings become available through coordinated disclosure, the next step is for robotics manufacturers is to connect each finding to its potential effect on development, deployment, and robot behavior.
That work also requires understanding how threats could affect robot behavior and how to protect systems already in operation. VicOne Radeis helps teams identify potential zero-day vulnerabilities, assess AI model and system security, and use simulation to evaluate how these risks could affect robot behavior before deployment. VicOne Rthena supports threat detection and responses within approved policies during operation.
Figure 2. Cybersecurity strengthens robot safety evidence throughout the lifecycle. VicOne helps teams test safety limits against manipulation before deployment and monitor the conditions behind safe behavior in operation.VicOne
Faster vulnerability discovery matters when teams can turn findings into action: identify what needs attention, verify that safeguards still hold, and confirm that a fix does not introduce new risks. That is how cybersecurity strengthens robot safety as systems continue to change.
For a deeper look how cybersecurity can affect robot safety, download our white paper, “Why Robot Safety Depends on Cybersecurity: Protecting the Information That Safety Decisions Rely On.”
VicOne is a Physical AI cybersecurity company protecting vehicles and robots from cyber threats that can alter behavior and compromise safety. Headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, the company provides automotive and robotics organizations with software and services to identify cyber risks early, assess their potential safety impact, and protect systems in operation, helping maintain safe, reliable behavior across real-world deployments.
