title: US firm to support development of new propellants to boost aircraft range
content: A Salt Lake City-based company has received a contract from the Department of War to to advance the development of alternative fuel sources. With the $86.3 million award, CycloKinetics will work to advance alternative fuels. “At CycloKinetics we believe that persistent U.S. military superiority depends on airpower resiliency and, to that end, advanced propellants are a decisive tactical and strategic advantage,” said Mukund Karanjikar, CEO and founder of CycloKinetics.“We develop propellants that materially impact the range, payload, speed, and trajectory of both current and future aircraft, missiles, and rockets.” Advanced, drop-in replacement fuels and propellantsThe latest contract will support the development of advanced, high-performance propellants designed to enhance aircraft range, missile capabilities and space launch performance.CycloKinetics specializes in developing advanced, drop-in replacement fuels and propellants for aerospace and defense applications. Its proprietary technologies are designed to deliver improved energy performance while remaining compatible with existing propulsion systems.The award highlights the growing importance of advanced fuel technologies in strengthening military readiness, extending operational range and reducing dependence on conventional fuel systems.“The U.S. Department of War’s awarding to CycloKinetics reflects this administration’s relentless approach to improving the readiness of our Armed Forces. CycloKinetics’ fuel performance contributions significantly improve America’s ability to neutralize enemy forces, in the air, land, sea, space, cyber and nuclear domains,” said Gen. Tod Wolters, CycloKinetics Board Member and retired U.S. Air Force four-star general who served as Commander of the U.S. European Command and NATO’s Supreme Allied Commander Europe (SACEUR).The award comes as the US military continues to explore technologies that can improve operational resilience and strengthen its aerospace capabilities.Advanced propellants could provide strategic advantagesAdvanced propellants could provide strategic advantages by increasing aircraft endurance, extending missile range and reducing the need for frequent refuelling.In its announcement, CycloKinetics emphasized that improved propulsion technologies could play an important role in maintaining US military superiority across multiple operational domains.“By recognizing propellants as a strategic advantage, the U.S. can extend operational reach, reduce refueling dependencies, and maintain a decisive technological overmatch. The key to ensuring future air superiority lies in advanced propellants that power existing and emerging aircraft to victory and we’re honored to be recognized by the U.S. Department of War as a partner in this mission,” added Karanjikar.The development of higher-energy-density propellants could have implications for military aviation, missile systems and space launch operations, particularly where range, payload capacity and operational endurance are critical.The next major challenge will be translating the technology’s reported performance advantages into scalable, commercially viable production.As the aerospace and defense industries continue to prioritize advanced propulsion systems and energy resilience, CycloKinetics’ latest award places the company in a notable position within the evolving market for next-generation aerospace fuels.

title: US researchers built open-source chip for smarter wearable devices
content: Researchers at the New Jersey Institute of Technology (NJIT) and collaborating institutions have developed an open-source microcontroller that combines sensing, wireless connectivity, onboard storage, and battery management into a device about the size of a quarter, opening the door to compact wearables, robotic systems, and other connected electronics.They named it TinZr (pronounced “TIN-zer”), which is the square-shaped microcontroller that measures just 0.98 inches (2.5 centimeters) on each side. Despite its compact footprint, it integrates an inertial measurement unit (IMU) for tracking motion and orientation, a microSD card reader for local data storage, a battery management circuit, and built-in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth connectivity.Researchers positioned TinZr as a flexible, open-source system that can be adapted for a range of applications covering physiological monitoring to robotics and industrial sensing.Built to simplify wearable electronicsMicrocontrollers act as the central processing units of many embedded devices that can collect information from sensors, store data, and communicate with other electronics. However, combining all of these functions into a compact board often requires engineers to compromise on size or capability.According to the researchers, the chip was designed to overcome those limitations by integrating multiple functions into a single miniature platform without significantly increasing its footprint. Besides keeping it tiny, the the microcontroller has wireless connectivity; the board supports analog, digital, and serial communication interfaces through general-purpose input/output (GPIO) pins. Together, these features could let developers connect a wide variety of external sensors.Lead author Ludvik Alkhoury, who completed his doctoral research at NJIT and is now a postdoctoral associate at Weill Cornell Medicine, said the team could not find an existing microcontroller that combined the required size, form factor, and functionality.“You couldn’t find anything on the market that has the same size, same form factor, and also has all the functionalities that we wanted,” Alkhoury said.The project originated while researchers were developing a wearable oximeter for the U.S. Navy to monitor pilots’ heart rate and blood oxygen levels amid high-speed maneuvers that can cause pilots to lose consciousness. Those strict size and weight constraints ultimately led the team to design an even smaller and more versatile electronics platform.Designed as flexible research platformWith onboard battery management, wireless communications, and removable storage, TinZr can continuously collect data from attached sensors without relying on external hardware. The researchers described it as a general-purpose data acquisition platform that can be customized for many different scientific and engineering projects.Potential applications could go far beyond wearable health monitors. The team envisions the device monitoring brain activity in laboratory animals, measuring movement and physical strain in construction workers. They also hope to use the device to coordinate swarms of drones and support robotics research that requires compact, low-power electronics.The researchers have made the quarter-sized controller fully open source to encourage wider adoption. Its Arduino software library is available on GitHub, while printed circuit board designs, component lists, and 3D-printable enclosure files are available through the Zenodo research repository. This allows engineers to modify both the hardware and software to suit specialized applications.Rather than targeting a single use case, the developers hope TinZr will form a foundation for new wearable technologies, sensor platforms, and robotic systems that benefit from combining wireless communication, onboard storage, and sensor integration in a compact, customizable package.The researcher described the platform in the journal HardwareX.

title: US scales up production of truck-transportable nuclear microreactors
content: A new generation of transportable nuclear reactors is moving closer to commercial production in the United States. Two manufacturing sites in California and Tennessee will support the production and fueling of 1-megawatt microreactors. Their development targets initial customer deliveries in 2028, with eventual capacity reaching hundreds of units annually.Radiant plans to invest more than $380 million across the two locations. The expansion will support its Kaleidos reactor, which uses a factory-built design intended for transport by truck. Its production strategy also includes an unusual capability: fueling reactors at a private facility before shipping them to customers.Two sites, different rolesThe expanded El Segundo, California, headquarters will serve as the primary assembly and engineering center. Radiant has committed more than $100 million to its Los Angeles-area operations. The expansion adds approximately 200,000 square feet of manufacturing and research space.Engineers will use the facility to assemble multiple reactors simultaneously. Its equipment includes bridge cranes and dedicated testing infrastructure for reactor control systems. Radiant will also manufacture turbomachinery and power-generation equipment in-house.The facility has already produced the first Kaleidos reactor. That unit is currently at Idaho National Laboratory, where it will undergo testing. The expanded production space will help engineers move from individual reactor builds toward repeatable manufacturing.Tennessee will handle another critical part of the process. Radiant is developing an 81-acre campus in Oak Ridge for reactor manufacturing, fueling, and storage. The project represents an additional investment of approximately $280 million.Its fueling infrastructure will allow Radiant to prepare sealed reactors before transporting them to customer locations. This approach could simplify deployment for military installations and commercial facilities. Customers would not need conventional underground construction to establish an on-site nuclear installation.Commercial orders take shapeRadiant has already attracted customers across military and commercial markets. The U.S. Army awarded the company up to $750 million to develop and deploy 15 Kaleidos reactors. Initial deliveries are planned for 2028, with all 15 units expected by 2030.The Department of the Air Force selected Radiant for a microreactor project at Buckley Space Force Base in Colorado. The Navy also chose the company to support energy independence at Naval Weapons Station Crane in Indiana. Commercial data center operator Equinix has separately agreed to purchase 20 units.Testing and fuel supplyThe company is also preparing Kaleidos for full-scale testing at Idaho National Laboratory’s DOME facility. The program will evaluate the same reactor design intended for commercial customers. Testing will examine sustained full-power operation, autonomous controls, and performance at operating temperatures.The Department of Energy has approved the reactor’s Documented Safety Analysis. Kaleidos is now undergoing the DOE’s Readiness Review ahead of its planned full-power test campaign.Fuel availability represents another important part of the production plan. Radiant has secured Department of Energy HALEU allocations and enrichment agreements with Urenco and Centrus Energy. It also signed a multiton TRISO fuel supply agreement with Standard Nuclear extending into the early 2030s.

title: US to boost missile defense, new sensor to modernize seeker tech
content: A Virginia-based company has received contract to develop advanced next-generation sensor for the Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) interceptor missile. Leonardo DRS has received this contract from BAE Systems.Leonardo will develop the next-generation infrared focal plane array for THAAD, which remains a critical element of U.S. missile defense architecture, and the next-generation seeker technology is intended to enhance the interceptor’s ability to address evolving and increasingly complex threats.Vital missile defense mission“Leonardo DRS is continuing to expand its role in the munitions seeker market through recent wins that leverage both cooled and uncooled solutions at the detector, sensor and subsystem levels,” said Jerry Hathaway, senior vice president and general manager of DRS Electro-Optical and Infrared Systems. “THAAD is an important strategic program for our company, and we are proud to support this vital missile defense mission. Our ability to combine high-end performance with scalable, cost-effective production makes Leonardo DRS a strong partner for a wide range of mission requirements.”DRS is a leading provider of advanced cooled and uncooled infrared systems for the U.S. government and allied nations worldwide. The company delivers deployed mission capabilities across ground, sea, air and space domains. Advanced sensing technologies remain a key strategic focus for DRS as it integrates its multi-domain sensing expertise with secure communications and laser technologies to support critical national security missions, including missile defense, counter-unmanned aircraft systems, autonomous maritime protection and ground combat operations, according to a press release. Advanced infrared sensing technology for THAAD missilesThe new contract will support the development of advanced infrared sensing technology, while the company expands its Dallas manufacturing capacity to meet growing demand for THAAD interceptor seekers.The next-generation infrared focal plane array is intended to enhance the sensing capabilities of the THAAD interceptor’s seeker. Infrared sensing technology enables defence systems to detect and track objects through their thermal signatures, providing an important capability in challenging operational environments.By developing an advanced generation of infrared sensing technology, Leonardo DRS aims to support the evolving requirements of the THAAD programme as missile defense systems face increasingly complex threats.Leonardo DRS brings expertise in cooled and uncooled infrared technologies, including detectors, sensors and integrated subsystems. Its expanding presence in the munitions seeker market reflects a broader strategy to deliver high-performance sensing solutions for a range of defence applications.As the demand for advanced missile defence solutions continues to evolve, the programme highlights the growing role of high-performance infrared sensors and scalable manufacturing in supporting future national security requirements.As military requirements evolve, defense programmes are placing greater importance on technologies that combine high performance with reliable, scalable production.For Leonardo DRS, the THAAD-related development programme represents an opportunity to strengthen its position in the advanced infrared sensing and munitions seeker markets while supporting a major US missile defence programme.THAAD provides a transportable, rapidly deployable ground-based regional missile defense capability to intercept and destroy short, medium, and intermediate-range ballistic missiles in the terminal or final phase of flight.THAAD is designed to intercept threats both inside and outside the Earth’s atmosphere providing a critical capability for defense against ballistic missile attacks. The system is mobile, rapidly deployable and able to defend military, allied forces, citizen population centers, critical infrastructure and other critical assets anywhere in the world within hours.

title: Video: New underwater robot dives 328 feet deep to spot hull damage
content: A Chinese underwater robot that lets boat owners inspect propellers, check hull damage, and explore submerged areas without getting wet is now available for $3,499.Developed by underwater robotics specialist QYSEA, the FIFISH V6 EXPERT is a tethered remotely operated vehicle (ROV) with a modular design that includes detachable components for its motor, lighting, camera, and battery.The system combines 4K cameras, multidirectional movement, and an optional robotic arm to capture footage and handle small objects underwater. The system allows users to investigate potential damage, check for tangled ropes, and examine submerged objects from the surface. Robotic diving expertDesigned to operate in environments that are difficult or unsafe for divers to access, the ROV combines a high-definition camera, six degrees of freedom (6-DOF) movement, powerful LED lighting, and compatibility with several underwater tools. It can descend to depths of up to 100 meters (328 feet), allowing users to examine boat hulls, propellers, underwater structures, and other submerged objects.The robot measures 38.3 centimeters long, 33.1 centimeters wide, and 14.3 centimeters high. It weighs approximately 4.6 kilograms (10.14 pounds), making it relatively compact for transportation and deployment. Its propulsion system uses multiple thrusters to provide movement in six directions: forward and backward, left and right, and up and down. It can also rotate through 360 degrees in yaw, pitch, and roll, allowing it to change orientation without needing to turn around. QYSEA lists its maximum speed at 3 knots (1.5 meters per second).The V6 EXPERT uses a 1/2.3-inch Sony CMOS image sensor with 12-megapixel resolution and an f/2.5 lens. Its camera offers a 166-degree field of view above water and a 96-degree field of view underwater. It can record 4K video at 25 or 30 frames per second, while 1080p footage can be captured at up to 120 frames per second. To improve visibility in dark underwater environments, the ROV carries two LED lights producing a combined 6,000 lumens. The lights have a 5,500K color temperature and a 120-degree beam angle. Users can save footage and photographs using its removable microSD storage system, which comes with a 128GB card and supports cards up to 256GB according to QYSEA’s current specifications.Precision diving technologyThe robot also incorporates onboard sensors to help maintain its position and orientation underwater. These include a gyroscope, accelerometer, magnetometer, depth sensor, and temperature sensor. According to the firm, its depth-lock function can maintain a selected depth with an accuracy of approximately ±1 centimeter, helping the vehicle remain steady while inspecting a particular section of a boat or underwater structure. Other intelligent features include Vision Lock, Diver Tracking, and Q-STEADY 2.0 stabilization technology. Arm+1Power comes from a 156Wh battery, with an operating duration of approximately one to four hours depending on working conditions. QYSEA also advertises fast charging, with the battery reaching 90 percent capacity in about an hour, although actual charging times can vary. An optional Onshore Power Supply System (OPSS) allows extended operations using a surface-based power source rather than relying entirely on the onboard battery.The V6 EXPERT connects to its surface controller through a tether cable available in 100-meter (328-foot) and 200-meter (656-foot) configurations. The cable has a tensile strength of 100 kilogram-force and neutral buoyancy underwater, helping prevent it from pulling the vehicle down or interfering with its movement. The remote controller uses 5GHz Wi-Fi connectivity and offers up to four hours of operating time.One of its most useful features is the Q-IF interface, which supports additional equipment for different underwater tasks. Compatible accessories include a robotic arm with parallel grippers for retrieving objects, a retrieval hook, a 2D imaging sonar for locating objects in poor visibility, and measurement tools such as laser scalers and distance meters. Water-quality sensors can also measure dissolved oxygen, salinity, turbidity, and pH. For boat owners, the robotic arm is particularly useful for handling small objects, while the camera provides a closer look at damaged or obstructed areas. However, the robot’s capabilities depend on the accessories fitted and underwater conditions.

content:
Jinko Solar's perovskite/TOPCon tandem cell reaches 35.24% efficiency
JinkoSolar
has announced that its N-type TOPCon-based perovskite tandem cell has reached a conversion efficiency above 35.24%, certified by the Shanghai Institute of Microsystem and Information Technology of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. The result is up from the
the company reported about five months earlier for the same type of cell. In May, Jinko’s R&D director had
presented a 34.76% cell
. Jinko counts the new result as its 34th record for cell efficiency and module power.
The company credits selective passivation for textured silicon surfaces in its TOPCon cells, a multi-component crystallization control strategy for the perovskite layer, nanoscale interface passivation materials, and improved light management.
JinkoSolar sees its continuous efficiency improvements as proof that the perovskite/TOPCon tandem route is steadily maturing in terms of efficiency and engineering validation. In its own words, it has set a new efficiency benchmark for this technology route, accumulated technological momentum for subsequent industrialization, and strengthened industry confidence.

title: Perovskite cells made without toxic solvents keep 96% of efficiency over 2,000 hours
content:
Perovskite cells made without toxic solvents keep 96% of efficiency over 2,000 hours
Researchers at the University of Waterloo and the University of Konstanz have developed inverted perovskite solar cells in which every solution-processed layer is made with green solvents. The cells reach a power conversion efficiency of up to 19.1% and hold up well under heat and continuous operation.
Most high-efficiency perovskite cells use toxic solvents such as DMF and NMP for the perovskite layer, and chlorobenzene for the charge transport layers. Efforts to replace them have usually tackled only one layer. The team, whose work builds on earlier green-solvent efforts such as a
Swansea University team’s use of the same GVL solvent
in printed carbon cells, built the perovskite layer from the green solvent γ-valerolactone (GVL). They mixed in 10% to 20% DMSO as a co-solvent to slow crystallization. GVL alone gave films with wrinkles and pinholes, which shorted many cells. In the finished stack, the self-assembled monolayers are dissolved in isopropanol and the C60 and BCP layers are thermally evaporated, so no toxic solvent is used anywhere.
The researchers also added poly(4-fluorostyrene), a polymer that interacts with the perovskite precursors, slowing crystallization and producing larger grains. According to the paper, it also lowers trap density by about 20% and suppresses ion migration. Hysteresis fell from 2.97% to 0.56%, and the champion efficiency rose from 18.16% for the control to 19.1%.
The biggest gains were in stability:
after about 1,000 hours of storage at 65 °C, the polymer-treated cells kept 98% of their initial efficiency, against 88% for the control.
Operation:
after 2,000 hours of continuous maximum power point tracking, they kept 96%. The control kept 85% after 1,960 hours.
Ambient storage:
after 1,600 hours, they kept about 95%, against 50% for the control.
Temperature-dependent X-ray diffraction showed the polymer pushing the onset of thermal degradation of the perovskite from about 185 °C to between 220 °C and 250 °C. The authors say the stability is among the best reported for inverted cells made entirely with green solvents.

title: Stronger interface anchoring helps perovskite cells survive temperature swings
content:
Stronger interface anchoring helps perovskite cells survive temperature swings
Researchers at Henan University, the University of Naples Federico II, the University of Cambridge, Queen Mary University of London, the University of Stuttgart, the Instituto de Tecnologia Quimica (CSIC-Universitat Politecnica de Valencia), Polymat at the University of the Basque Country, Cardiff University, Henan Normal University, Xiamen University, China Jiliang University, Southeast University, Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin and Bielefeld University have developed a surface pretreatment that makes the buried interface of inverted perovskite solar cells more resistant to temperature cycling.
Indium chloride-treated ITO surface and SAM anchoring. Image credit: Wu et al., Science Advances (2026)
Inverted cells commonly use a self-assembled monolayer (SAM) as the hole-selective contact on a transparent conductive oxide such as ITO. The team says that under temperature swings, thermal expansion mismatch between the layers builds up stress at this interface and weakens adhesion, even without significant chemical degradation. In an untreated stack, the interfacial fracture energy fell from 1.59 to 0.50 J/m² after aging, a 69% reduction. To address this, the researchers treat the ITO with indium chloride before depositing the SAM. The treatment increases the density of hydroxyl groups on the surface and introduces chloride, which the authors say lets the SAM molecules anchor at several points, through metal-oxygen coordination supported by chloride-induced hydrogen bonding. Calculations for two SAM molecules, MeO-2PACz and m-PhPACz, showed stronger adsorption on the treated surface.
The best small-area device (7.81 mm²) reached a power conversion efficiency of 27.3%, certified at 26.9%. A 1 cm² cell reached 25.7%, and a module with a 70 cm² aperture area reached 22.7%. After 400 temperature cycles between -40 and 85°C (ISOS-T-3), the treated devices retained 94% of their initial efficiency, compared with 59% for the control. They also retained 95% after 2,000 hours of continuous illumination with maximum power point tracking, and 95% after 1,000 hours of heating at 85°C.
Thermal stress has been a recurring theme in this line of work. An
earlier study
involving a team led by Meng Li at Henan University found it to be the decisive factor in the degradation of metal-halide perovskites. Preparing the ITO surface for better SAM anchoring has also been
explored before

title: China grid-connects world’s first artificial-cavern CAES plant - pv magazine Global
content:
Applications & Installations
The 300 MW/1.8 GWh project uses excavated hard-rock chambers, expanding compressed-air storage options beyond natural salt caverns.
Vincent Shaw
20 Nov 2026
Applications & Installations
Energy Storage
Yuanchu No. 1 compressed air energy storage (CAES) station in Yumen, Gansu province
China’s Yuanchu No. 1 compressed air energy storage (CAES) station in Yumen, Gansu province, achieved its first grid connection on November 16, marking what its developer describes as the world’s first grid-connected CAES facility using purpose-excavated underground rock caverns.
The project was developed by China Energy Digital Technology Group, a subsidiary of China Energy Engineering Corporation, which is responsible for its investment, construction, and operation.
Rated at 300 MW/1,800 MWh, the facility is designed for an eight-hour charging cycle and six hours of continuous discharge. Total investment reached approximately CNY 2.5 billion ($368 million), with projected annual electricity generation of 600 GWh.
Its defining feature is an engineered underground air storage system. Four interconnected chambers were excavated approximately 110 meters below the surface in hard rock, creating a pressurized storage space of around 200,000 cubic meters. The system has a design pressure of 18 MPa.
The plant employs non-combustion, adiabatic CAES technology. During charging, electricity drives compressors that pressurize air, while heat generated during compression is recovered and stored. During discharge, the stored heat reheats the compressed air before expansion through turbines, eliminating the need for supplementary natural gas combustion.
According to molten-salt supplier Shandong Huayang Dier Chemical, the thermal system combines low-melting-point ternary molten salt with pressurized hot water to recover and store heat at different temperatures. Lower- and medium-temperature compression heat is stored in pressurized water tanks, while higher-temperature heat is transferred to molten-salt tanks. During discharge, both media release heat in stages to reheat the air before expansion. The developer also reports using shared heat-exchange equipment during charging and discharging, reducing equipment duplication.
The developer reports a round-trip electrical efficiency of 72%, although sustained operational data have not yet independently confirmed the figure.
The artificial-cavern approach addresses a geographical constraint on CAES deployment. Salt caverns offer relatively economical underground storage but require suitable geological formations. Excavating and sealing chambers in competent hard rock could broaden site selection, although geological conditions and construction costs remain important considerations.
Yumen lies within the Hexi Corridor, a major wind and solar development region in northwest China. The plant is intended to absorb surplus renewable electricity during off-peak periods and return it to the grid when demand rises, providing multi-hour balancing capacity.
China has been expanding its large-scale CAES fleet. At least six projects rated at 100 MW or above have been reported as grid-connected, including the 600 MW Huai’an salt-cavern station, the 700 MW Jintan Phase II project, 300 MW facilities in Yingcheng and Feicheng, the 100 MW Zhangjiakou demonstration project and Yuanchu No. 1.
According to an October 2026 report by the Energy Storage Application Branch of the China Industrial Association of Power Sources, 13 CAES projects were under construction, totaling 4.95 GW/23.95 GWh. Separately, industry figures cited in November indicated more than 36 GW of projects in preparation as of the first quarter of 2026, with nearly 100 project filings nationwide.
The figures highlight China’s growing CAES pipeline, although many proposed projects remain subject to financing, geological assessments and commercial viability. For Yuanchu No. 1, long-term efficiency, cavern integrity and operating costs will determine whether artificial-cavern technology can be replicated economically.

title: China's TOPCon solar module export prices slip as makers clear low-efficiency stock ahead of new standard - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
In a new weekly update for
pv magazine
, OPIS, a Dow Jones company, provides a quick look at the main price trends in the global PV industry.
20 Nov 2026
Markets & Policy
Free-On-Board (FOB) China mainstream module prices edged lower this week, weighed down by continued price weakness in lower-efficiency modules, as manufacturers clear inventories ahead of a stricter module efficiency standard taking effect on Jan. 1, 2027.
According to the OPIS Global Solar Markets Report released on Nov. 17, the Chinese Module Marker (CMM), the OPIS benchmark assessment for TOPCon modules below 645 W from China, fell 0.93% on the week to $0.106/W FOB China, after five consecutive weeks unchanged at $0.107/W.
Forward prices for Q1 2027 loading tracked the weakness in the spot module market, falling 0.93% week on week to $0.106/W, while Q2 through Q4 2027 held steady at $0.105/W.
Across efficiency grades, price indications for high-efficiency TOPCon modules, defined as products above 650 W, were heard in the low $0.110s/W, while back-contact modules were heard in the low-to-mid $0.110s/W. By contrast, a Dow Jones Energy market survey showed that lower-efficiency TOPCon modules, particularly those in the 625-630 W range, were quoted in the low $0.100s/W on an FOB China basis, with prices in some regions already falling below $0.100/W.
Industry sources noted that manufacturers have stepped up inventory clearance efforts in the fourth quarter, anticipating weaker domestic offtake for lower-efficiency modules once the new standard comes into effect. Under the standard, the minimum efficiency for TOPCon modules sold in China will be 23.2%, corresponding to a power output of 630 W.
Major producers’ inventories of lower-efficiency modules are already running low, one leading manufacturer said, as most have shifted production lines toward higher-efficiency products and average module power ratings among major TOPCon producers have reached around 640 W. Most of the remaining lower-efficiency stock sits with smaller or tier-2 players, who are undercutting prices aggressively, the manufacturer said.
A top-tier integrated module manufacturer said aggressive discounting in the lower-efficiency segment has also placed downward pressure on mainstream module prices, as procurement teams increasingly use lower-priced offers as leverage in price negotiations. The manufacturer added that while policies aimed at curbing module oversupply and regulating prices could support the market over the longer term, intense price competition among manufacturers is likely to persist in the near term.
Meanwhile, a divergence between domestic and export module prices has become increasingly evident since the start of Q4 2026.
Domestic mainstream TOPCon module prices have softened amid weakening demand, while export prices have remained comparatively resilient, with market sources noting that manufacturers’ quotations for overseas markets have largely resisted the downward trend in domestic prices.
According to OPIS data, EXW China TOPCon module prices fell by more than 1.8% since the beginning of October, while FOB China TOPCon mainstream modules remained broadly unchanged, before edging down by 0.93% this week.
In domestic tenders, China Energy Engineering Corporation (CEEC) shortlisted 23 bidders for its 2026 centralized module procurement tender, covering 15 GW of TOPCon, heterojunction (HJT) and back-contact modules. TOPCon modules accounted for the largest share at 10.7 GW, with shortlisted bids of CNY 0.695-0.770 ($0.104-0.115)/W. Back-contact modules represented 3.3 GW, with six companies shortlisted and bids of CNY 0.760-0.779/W, while HJT modules accounted for the remaining 1 GW, with bids of CNY 0.717-0.752/W.
OPIS is a specialist business within Dow Jones Energy, a global energy intelligence business that brings together trusted price reporting, research and market intelligence across the energy value chain. OPIS publishes the
OPIS Global Solar Markets Service
, which includes pricing data for solar panels and components across Asia, Europe and the U.S., manufacturing capacity data, module forward curves, and a global solar policy tracker.

title: Chinese PV Industry Brief: China Three Gorges opens 5.24 GW solar module tender - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
China Three Gorges has opened bidding for 5.24 GW of solar modules for 2027, while TCL Zhonghuan plans to increase its stake in a semiconductor subsidiary. In other news, Longi has secured a module supply deal in Australia, and China is stepping up efforts to recycle retired PV panels.
Vincent Shaw
20 Nov 2026
Markets & Policy
China Three Gorges Corp.
has opened bidding for its first centralized PV module procurement round for 2027, covering an estimated 5.24 GW. The tender attracted 20 bidders, with an average offer of CNY 0.7491 ($0.110)/W. Bids ranged from CNY 0.7088/W to CNY 0.7981/W. The tender requires modules to meet Grade 3 or higher energy-efficiency requirements under China’s GB 47834 standard. Final contract awards have yet to be announced. China Three Gorges
previously awarded contracts under its 2024 centralized module procurement program
China’s National Energy Administration (NEA)
said the country added 110.329 GW of grid-connected solar capacity in the first nine months of 2026, including 45.80 GW of utility-scale PV and 64.52 GW of distributed solar, of which 33.46 GW came from residential installations. Cumulative grid-connected solar capacity reached 1.31 TW at the end of September, with Jiangsu, Henan and Yunnan recording the largest additions. The figures follow an
earlier NEA report showing a sharp year-on-year decline in solar installations
China’s Ministry of Commerce
(Mofcom)
, together with eight other government agencies, has issued guidelines to strengthen the country’s recycling system, identifying retired PV modules, power batteries and wind turbine blades as priority areas. The policy encourages market-based cooperation between state-owned power companies and recycling enterprises, alongside the expansion of collection networks and recycling facilities. Authorities also plan to develop specific regulations for the recycling and disposal of decommissioned PV modules. China
previously outlined plans to establish a recycling system for retired solar panels and wind turbines
TCL Zhonghuan
has proposed acquiring an additional 65.80% stake in Zhonghuan Leading Semiconductor Technology through a share issuance, increasing its ownership from 32.72% to 98.52% upon completion. At a media briefing, the company reaffirmed solar and semiconductor materials as its two core businesses. It said its solar operations would focus on scaling back-contact (BC) technology and expanding internationally, with no plans for significant new wafer manufacturing capacity in the near term. TCL Zhonghuan
previously announced plans to convert 20 GW of TOPCon cell capacity to BC technology
has signed an agreement to supply 176 MW of Hi-MO 9 back-contact modules for the Muswellbrook solar-plus-storage project in New South Wales, Australia. Developed by OX2 at a rehabilitated former coal mine, the project will include a 100 MWh battery energy storage system. Grid connection is expected in 2028, with annual solar generation estimated at 347 GWh. The project forms part of a
broader renewable energy development at the former Muswellbrook coal mine
JA Solar
has launched an integrated solar-and-storage ecosystem in Chengdu, China, combining PV generation, battery storage, energy management and unified operations and maintenance services. The company claims the solution could improve system efficiency by 2% to 3%, cut installation and commissioning times by 20% to 30%, and reduce lifecycle project management costs by approximately 30% compared with systems assembled from separately supplied equipment. The projected benefits have not yet been independently verified through operational data. JA Solar
previously announced a broader strategy covering solar, storage and integrated energy services
has secured a tracker supply contract for the 500 MW Al Kamil I solar project in Oman. The Chinese manufacturer will supply its SkyLine II tracking system, which uses multi-point parallel-drive technology and is designed to withstand wind speeds exceeding 56 meters per second. Arctech said the system is engineered to improve structural stability and long-term reliability in high-wind desert environments. The company
previously secured tracker supply agreements for a 2.1 GW solar project in the United Arab Emirates
showcased an upgraded 4.8 MW SG4800UD-MV-US modular inverter at RE+ 2026 in the United States and publicly presented footage of a large-scale fire test of its PowerTitan 3.0 battery storage system for the first time. The company also displayed integrated power solutions for artificial intelligence (AI) data centers, including 800 V DC power supply technology and battery energy storage architectures, as it expands into computing infrastructure applications. Sungrow
previously introduced its PowerTitan 3.0 storage platform
TrendForce
said polysilicon inventories in China remained above 570,000 metric tons, with domestic production expected to fall to approximately 95,000 metric tons in November. Supply continues to slightly exceed downstream demand despite production cuts. Wafer inventories stood at around 27 GW, while prices for 183 mm, 210R and 210N wafers fell to CNY 0.93 ($0.137), CNY 0.98 ($0.144) and CNY 1.08 ($0.159) per piece, respectively. Some polysilicon offers have fallen below CNY 40 ($5.88)/kg, as weak demand and persistent inventories continue to weigh on prices across the solar supply chain. The latest figures follow
earlier reports of elevated polysilicon inventories and weak wafer demand

title: Enphase highlights new batteries, bidirectional charging - pv magazine Global
content:
Technology & Products
Enphase is rolling out residential and commercial storage, meter-collared vehicle-to-grid charging, and a medium-voltage solid-state transformer.
Ryan Kennedy
20 Nov 2026
Technology & Products
Energy Storage
Inverters
Residential
Enphase Energy is expanding its hardware lineup across home systems, commercial buildings, and high-power AI infrastructure. The company
exhibited
its new products at RE+ Las Vegas 2026.
“RE+ is where installers, developers, and utilities see the full Enphase platform in one place,” said Ken Fong, senior vice president of sales at Enphase Energy. “This year, that platform runs from the home to the commercial rooftop to data center applications and beyond, all built on the same distributed, semiconductor-based architecture.”
IQ Battery G5
The IQ Battery G5 was built to pack more home storage into a tighter, stackable footprint than earlier generations. Each 5 kWh AC-coupled module includes its own grid-forming microinverter and prismatic lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells.
Stacks scale up to 30 kWh across six blocks on a floor stand or 20 kWh across four blocks on a wall mount, with full installations scaling up to 100 kWh. Each block weighs 115.3 lbs with an IP67 enclosure, and the paired Wiring Block weighs 19.8 lbs with a NEMA-3R enclosure.
The battery carries a 15-year limited warranty, with pilots planned in Q4 2026 and volume shipments starting in Q1 2027.
IQ Bidirectional EV Charger
Enphase built the DC-based IQ Bidirectional EV Charger to let electric vehicles power a home or send energy back to the grid through a simpler meter-collar connection. It supports vehicle-to-home and vehicle-to-grid operation and carries a 10-year limited warranty.
Pilots are expected to start in Q4 2026, followed by volume shipments in Q1 2027.
IQ Battery C80
Commercial buildings are the target for the IQ Battery C80, Enphase’s first commercial battery system, which brings modular AC-coupled storage to businesses. It gives the company an entry point into commercial peak demand charge management, backup power, and solar-plus-storage projects as residential solar growth slows.
Each enclosure delivers 80 kWh of energy capacity and scales up to 2 MWh per site. The C80 uses lithium iron phosphate (LFP) chemistry with 314 Ah prismatic cells and delivers over 90% AC round-trip efficiency.
It measures 36.2 in wide, 78.7 in high, and 32.3 in deep, weighs 2,645 lbs, and operates from -22°F to 131°F. It comes in 277Y/480 V and 120Y/208 V three-phase models and carries a 15-year or 7,000-cycle warranty.
Paired with IQ9N-3P and IQ9S-3P commercial microinverters, the system stays AC-coupled to simplify installation for commercial contractors. Product pilots begin in Q1 2027, with volume shipments scheduled for Q2 2027.
IQ Solid-State Transformer (IQ SST)
AI data centers are getting a direct medium-voltage to 800 VDC power conversion path with the IQ Solid-State Transformer (IQ SST), avoiding multi-stage step-down gear. The design targets data center power bottlenecks and fast compute load swings, while domestic module production in Arlington, Texas supports U.S. manufacturing goals against established industrial power rivals.
It converts 13.8 kV and 34.5 kV medium-voltage AC directly to 800 VDC, supporting both 800 VDC and ±400 VDC rack architectures. Each power module is rated at 5.5 kW with over 98.5% peak efficiency expected, a 250–500 kHz switching frequency, a custom 22 nm Kestrel control ASIC, and gallium nitride (GaN) power switching, weighing roughly 8 lbs with silicone potting.
Racks scale up to 5 MW with ambient-air cooling and up to 1,008 power modules in a delta configuration for AC/DC operation (or 1,008 AC/DC plus 672 DC/DC modules), while skids scale up to 10 MW. The modular hot-swap design targets 99.999% availability, sub-millisecond transient response, and a 10-year limited warranty.
Enphase demonstrated 13.8 kV AC to 800 VDC conversion in October 2026 and expects full-system demonstrations to finish by the end of 2026. Customer pilots are slated for 2027, followed by initial commercial shipments in 2028.
Additional hardware and software
Residential and commercial IQ9N microinverters, the IQ Meter Collar, the IQ Combiner 6C, and the upcoming IQ System Controller 4 round out home and commercial installations.
Other additions include the IQ EV Charger 2, an AC-based bidirectional charging option, the U.S. IQ Plugin Solar System, and the Enphase Air smart thermostat. Solargraf software also features unified residential and commercial workflows with built-in AI tools.

title: High pressure drives irradiance gains across South East Asia as Sichuan misses out - pv magazine Global
content:
Applications & Installations
In a new weekly update for pv magazine,
, a DNV company, reports that October 2026 saw solar irradiance exceed average levels by over 20% across southern China and Southeast Asia, driven by strong El Niño conditions, persistent high pressure, and reduced cloud cover. However, cloudiness in Sichuan and Chongqing, cold fronts, Typhoon Champi, and wildfire haze in Indonesia reduced solar irradiance in some areas.
20 Nov 2026
Applications & Installations
Utility-scale
October 2026 brought unusually sunny conditions across much of southern China and mainland South East Asia, with irradiance 20%+ above average in the strongest-affected areas, according to analysis using the
Solcast API
. Persistent high pressure over South East Asia and the South China Sea, alongside a very strong El Niño, suppressed rainfall and cloud. Sichuan and Chongqing missed much of the irradiance boost, while repeated cold fronts and Typhoon Champi interrupted the broader pattern farther north and east.
The strongest positive irradiance anomalies stretched across Yunnan, Guangxi, Guangdong and Hainan, through northern Indochina and into the Philippines. Rainfall was up to 6 millimeters per day below average across much of the same region, helping keep skies clearer. October rainfall in the
southern southwest was more than 50% below normal, with drought persisting in Yunnan, southwest Guizhou and southern Guangxi. Southern and central China were also more than 1.5 C warmer than average. Hong Kong recorded its warmest October, with a mean temperature of 27.6 C. A weaker
northeast monsoon and persistent high pressure helped limit the usual influx of moisture and cloud, reinforcing the sunnier pattern during a very strong El Niño.
Sichuan and Chongqing were a notable exception. While surrounding regions recorded positive irradiance anomalies, the basin saw slightly below-average irradiance for October. More easterly winds than usual and lower pressure over the Sichuan Basin helped keep cloud concentrated over the region, with the surrounding terrain and anomalously high pressure limiting its dispersal. The additional cloud coincided with neutral to slightly above-average rainfall in October, in contrast with the drier conditions surrounding the basin and farther south.
Farther north and east, repeated cold-air outbreaks brought periods of increased cloud and precipitation, interrupting the otherwise favourable irradiance conditions. China experienced six cold-air outbreaks during October, 2.4 more than average. These brought rain and snow across parts of northern and eastern China, with eastern Hebei and most of Beijing receiving 50–100 mm of precipitation from 15–23 October.
Typhoon Champi provided another interruption to the broader pattern. The storm formed on 11 October and reached winds near 215 km/h, affecting Taiwan, Japan and China. Cloud and rainfall associated with the system reduced irradiance as it moved through the region, with 62,400 people evacuated in Shanghai due to the conditions. October was particularly active for tropical weather overall, with eight tropical cyclones across the South China Sea and western North Pacific during the month.
Farther south, Sumatra and Kalimantan recorded below-average irradiance despite substantial rainfall deficits. Indonesia had recorded more than 1.06 million fire hotspots by 14 October, with widespread smoke and haze reducing incoming sunlight despite the otherwise dry conditions. Aerosol optical depth shows where the heaviest concentrations of smoke and haze occurred during the month.
produces these figures by tracking clouds and aerosols at 1-2km resolution globally, using satellite data and proprietary
AI/ML algorithms
. This data is used to drive irradiance models, enabling Solcast to calculate irradiance at high resolution, with typical bias of less than 2%, and also cloud-tracking forecasts. This data is used by more than 350 companies managing over 350 GW of solar assets globally.

title: JinkoSolar claims 35.24% efficiency for perovskite-silicon tandem solar cell - pv magazine Global
content:
Research & Development
The result was confirmed by the Shanghai Institute of Microsystem and Information Technology of the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
Emiliano Bellini
20 Nov 2026
Research & Development
Cells & modules
A perovskite-silicon solar cell developer by JinkoSolar
Chinese solar module manufacturer
JinkoSolar
has announced that it has achieved a power conversion efficiency of 35.24% for a perovskite-silicon tandem solar cell.
The company said the result was certified by the Shanghai Institute of Microsystem and Information Technology of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS). JinkoSolar previously achieved an
efficiency of 34.82% with the same cell configuration
“This efficiency breakthrough was made possible by multiple core technological innovations, including selective passivation technology for textured silicon surfaces in N-type TOPCon, a perovskite multi-component crystallization synchronization control strategy, and nanoscale interface passivation materials and light-management enhancement technologies,” the company said in a statement, adding that the efficiency improvement was achieved over five months.
The company did not disclose further technical details about the cell or the efficiency improvement.
The current world record for perovskite-silicon tandem solar cell efficiency is held by Chinese manufacturer Longi, which
achieved 35.5% efficiency
in July 2026. The result, obtained with a two-terminal tandem cell, was independently certified by the European Solar Test Installation (ESTI). It surpassed Longi’s previous certified record of 34.85%, announced in April 2025.
Longi also recently
reported an efficiency of 35.31%
for a tandem cell incorporating specially designed self-assembled molecules. Longi previously achieved a certified efficiency of 34.85% in April 2025 and an
efficiency of 34.3% for a large-area tandem cell measuring 261 cm²
In January 2026, Chinese module maker Trinasolar
achieved 32.6% efficiency
for a large-area tandem cell developed with Huairou Laboratory, with the result certified by Germany’s Fraunhofer Institute for Solar Energy Systems (Fraunhofer ISE).

title: Mexico's solar capacity could reach 43.8 GW by 2035 - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
GlobalData has raised its solar growth forecast for Mexico by 6 GW, citing a growing pipeline of renewable energy projects. However, grid congestion, transmission constraints and regulatory uncertainty could slow deployment.
Luis Ini
20 Nov 2026
Markets & Policy
Highlights
Utility-scale
The Villanueva PV plant in Mexico
Mexico’s installed solar capacity is expected to increase from 13.7 GW in 2025 to 43.8 GW by 2035, according to the latest report on the Mexican electricity market by research and consultancy firm GlobalData. The firm forecasts that renewables will account for 42.3% of the country’s total installed power capacity by 2035, up from 22.9% in 2025.
The latest projection represents an upward revision of 6 GW from GlobalData’s December 2025 forecast, which put Mexico’s installed solar capacity at 37.8 GW by 2035.
The Mexico Power Market Trends and Analysis by Capacity, Generation, Transmission, Distribution, Regulations, Key Players and Forecast to 2035 report projects that Mexico’s total installed power capacity will increase from 104.2 GW in 2025 to 156 GW in 2035, representing a compound annual growth rate of 4.1%. Over the same period, natural gas-fired generation capacity is expected to rise from 53.4 GW to 64.8 GW.
Despite the expansion of renewables, GlobalData expects thermal power plants to continue accounting for nearly 60% of Mexico’s electricity generation in 2035, while the share of renewables in the generation mix is projected to increase from 14.5% to 31.9%. The consultancy also forecasts that electricity consumption will rise from 328.5 TWh in 2025 to 423.2 TWh in 2035, driven by industrial nearshoring, the expansion of data centers, and growing demand for air conditioning.
Attaurrahman Ojindaram Saibasan, a power sector analyst at GlobalData, said the 2025 Electricity Sector Law and the binding nature of the 2025-2039 Electricity Sector Development Plan (PLADESE) have reshaped Mexico’s investment landscape. The new framework guarantees the state at least 54% of the electricity injected into the grid and gives a central role to mixed-investment projects involving the Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) and private companies.
Against this backdrop, the Mexican government announced in June its target of adding 22 GW of renewable energy capacity by 2030. The Ministry of Energy (Sener) recently reported the selection of 121 solar and wind projects totaling 18 GW. Meanwhile, CFE has increased planned investment in its portfolio of mixed-capital renewable energy projects to $10.6 billion. The portfolio includes 8,026 MW of generation capacity and more than 2,500 MW of energy storage capacity.
GlobalData has identified a pipeline of power generation projects exceeding 45 GW, dominated by solar PV. However, it warned that transmission and distribution losses, estimated at around 11.5%, and congestion on transmission lines connecting northern Mexico with demand centers in central Mexico and the Bajío region could slow the connection of new projects to the grid.
“Mexico is not lacking in projects or resources. The pace of the transition will depend on whether the mixed-investment model can attract international developers – following years of regulatory uncertainty – and on whether the CFE can expand transmission infrastructure quickly enough,” said Saibasan.

title: Proper Voltage, Unigrid unveil sodium-ion storage solution for data centers - pv magazine Global
content:
Technology & Products
The Salt Vault High Power cabinet aims to deliver some of the benefits of sodium-ion chemistries including the concept that rapid and repeated power transients may not degrade sodium-ion batteries as fast as lithium and lead-acid.
Tristan Rayner
20 Nov 2026
Technology & Products
Batteries
Energy Storage
California-based duo Proper Voltage and Unigrid have teamed up to pair voltage-control electronics with sodium-chromium oxide cells to create a 73.1 kWh backup cabinet aimed at delivering power to data centers.
Battery integration firm Proper Voltage announced that it has launched Salt Vault, an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) battery cabinet built around sodium-ion cells from San Diego-based
. Commercial deliveries to unnamed early-adopter data center and critical infrastructure operators are scheduled to begin in April 2027.
The system combines Proper Voltage’s software that it calls its battery operating system (bOS) with Unigrid’s sodium-chromium oxide (NCO) chemistry.
According to Proper Voltage’s product specifications, the Salt Vault High Power cabinet delivers 73.1 kWh of capacity and 333 kW of power output at a nominal 522 VDC, rated for 10,000 cycles. It operates across a discharge temperature range of -20 C to 40 C and a charge range of 0 C to 40 C. A single module in the cabinet is 6.1 kWh.
The two companies are targeting a specific operational problem in AI data centers, where training and inference clusters swing from idle to peak load in milliseconds. Those repeated power transients may accelerate degradation in conventional lead-acid and lithium iron phosphate (LFP) backup batteries.
Proper Voltage says its software-defined voltage control as part of its bOS regulates output across the full state of charge, allowing the sodium-ion cabinet to drop into existing UPS architectures without inverter redesigns. It can also adapt to 800 V racks, as the industry scales towards that voltage level.
No independent performance data or pricing has been disclosed.
“Performance is what drives the best models, and the battery behind them must be resilient and adaptive across every one of those demands,” said Charlie Welch, CEO of Proper Voltage. Unigrid CEO Darren Tan said the NCO chemistry is built for high-rate pulse power and thermal stability under heavy cycling.
The launch adds to a growing push by sodium-ion developers into AI infrastructure, where fire safety and high-rate discharge may matter more than energy density.
Earlier this year,
Energy Vault locked in 1.5 GWh of Peak Energy’s sodium-ion systems
for its AI data center portfolio.
And, less happily, ESS Tech introduced a
modular sodium-ion platform for the same market
in July, before it went out of business in November.
The hill to climb towards supplying hyperscalers is steep.
Nvidia’s BESS qualification program only Tesla, LG, and Hitachi,
underscoing how hard supply deals are for tier-one data center contracts.

title: The Hydrogen Stream: China starts operating 195 km hydrogen pipeline - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
In other news, ACME Group has approved a $3.6 billion green ammonia project in India, while researchers in Chile have assessed hydrogen production from curtailed renewable power. Qair has inaugurated a hydrogen plant in France, Plug Power has launched a utility-scale electrolyzer offering, and Protium has advanced two UK hydrogen projects.
Sergio Matalucci
20 Nov 2026
Markets & Policy
Energy Storage
Hydrogen
Utility-scale
has started operating a 195 km hydrogen pipeline connecting Darhan Muminggan United Banner with Baotou, Inner Mongolia, reported Xinhua News Agency. The pipeline has an approved annual transport capacity of 100,000 tons of hydrogen, potentially increasing to 240,000 tons. Developed by Inner Mongolia Huadian Huameng Pipeline, the infrastructure will connect renewable hydrogen production facilities in northern Baotou with industrial consumers in the south. Pipeline transport could reduce hydrogen delivery costs from about CNY 13 ($1.83)/kg by tube trailer to approximately CNY 3/kg, according to Xinhua. China has been
expanding its hydrogen transport infrastructure
to connect renewable energy resources with industrial demand.
ACME Group
has reached a final investment decision (FID) on a $3.6 billion green ammonia project in Odisha, India, with an annual production capacity of 760,000 tons. The facility, scheduled for commissioning in 2029, will feature a 2,200-ton-per-day ammonia production loop designed by Thyssenkrupp Uhde. It will use renewable electricity to produce hydrogen through electrolysis for green ammonia production, targeting customers in India, Japan and Europe. Brookfield has committed up to $600 million to support ACME’s green molecules platform. The project is expected to avoid more than 1.5 million tons of greenhouse gas emissions annually. ACME has also
secured green ammonia supply contracts in India
and is developing green methanol projects.
Researchers in Chile
have found that green hydrogen produced from curtailed solar electricity could achieve a levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) as low as $5.58/kg, compared with $7.27/kg for the most competitive wind projects. The study, “
Green hydrogen from curtailment: Real data analysis
,” assessed operational data from 56 solar plants and 44 wind farms with a combined capacity of 10.4 GW between July 2023 and June 2024. Curtailment occurred in about 25% of recorded hourly intervals, predominantly at low power levels. Using a techno-economic model based on proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzers, the researchers identified optimal electrolyzer capacities of 5% to 13% of the renewable plants’ net effective power across the 10 best-performing projects, all located in northern Chile. The projects achieved LCOH values of $5.58/kg to $6.97/kg, with electrolyzer capacity factors of 25% to 30%. Deviations of up to 50% from optimal electrolyzer sizing increased hydrogen production costs by no more than 3.8%. The study, to be published in
Energy Reports

title: Vietnam sets rooftop solar monitoring and control acceptance procedure - pv magazine Global
content: Vietnam’s state-owned national power utility Vietnam Electricity (EVN) has introduced new technical requirements and acceptance procedures for rooftop solar installations that export surplus electricity to the grid. Decision No. 1382/QĐ-EVN , issued on November 18, sets out technical specifications and a process for testing and accepting rooftop solar installations connected to EVN’s monitoring, data-collection and control systems. It replaces Decision No. 378/QĐ-EVN, issued on Mar. 12, 2025, and takes effect immediately. The requirements cover rooftop solar systems designed for self-consumption that export surplus electricity to the grid and fall within the electricity company’s monitoring and control remit. Under the specifications, installations must transmit operational data to the electricity company’s monitoring system, with inverter output updated at intervals of no more than five minutes. Systems must also be capable of both receiving and executing remote commands to limit exported power, as well as automatically adjusting inverter output to comply with instructions from the utility. The acceptance testing procedure includes documentation reviews, site inspections, communications testing and verification of monitoring and control signals. Utilities must also test a system’s ability to reduce exports in response to power limitation commands and check its behaviour during communications outages and faults before issuing any acceptance documentation. EVN says system owners are responsible for installing compatible monitoring, metering and communications equipment, providing technical documentation and coordinating with utilities during testing. Electricity companies are responsible for providing connection and communications configurations, verifying cybersecurity and monitoring functionality and conducting the acceptance tests. The decision comes as Vietnam looks to accelerate rooftop solar deployment. The Vietnamese government ordered provinces to speed up rooftop solar support policies in September. Last month, it called on provincial and municipal authorities to introduce these policies by the end of the year . A Ministry of Industry and Trade publication released in September also outlined plans to link distributed rooftop solar, behind-the-meter battery energy storage systems and electric vehicles into flexible grid assets , moving away from basic time-of-use tariffs. Vietnam’s solar capacity surpassed 19 GW by the end of 2025, with around 586 MW of solar added last year. The country had more than 11.45 GW of rooftop solar capacity across 134,410 installations as of the end of August 2026, according to figures from EVN. title: $64 solar-powered robot cleans PV modules without water - pv magazine Global
content:
A research team from Pakistan and China has developed a self-powered robotic system for cleaning photovoltaic panels in water-scarce regions. The low-cost system uses commercially available, off-the-shelf components and costs approximately $64 to build.
“The proposed approach was validated through a three-month field deployment in Bahawalpur, Pakistan, a high-soiling desert environment,” the researchers said. “By directly coupling cleaning actions to recoverable energy losses and emphasizing affordability, autonomy, and field validation, this work advances a practical framework for PV maintenance in water-scarce and resource-limited regions.”
The researchers built a prototype that uses two identical 5 V reference panels to determine when cleaning is required. A servo-driven wiper cleans one panel every 30 seconds, while the other accumulates dust. An ESP32 controller compares the panels’ voltages, with a difference of at least 2 V serving as the primary cleaning trigger. The system also monitors airborne dust concentrations, using a threshold of 250 µg/m³, and prevents cleaning when the module temperature exceeds 45 C.
Once activated, the 7.6 kg robot travels along the length of the PV module, while a motor-driven nylon roller brush cleans its full width. Ultrasonic sensors detect the module edges, while a dedicated 20 W solar panel charges the robot’s 12 V, 3 Ah battery.
The researchers tested the robot on a single 180 W monocrystalline silicon module measuring 1,480 mm × 670 mm, installed at a fixed tilt angle of 28 degrees. They recorded sensor readings and operating data at one-second intervals during the three-month field trial, which included dust storms and intermittent rainfall.
The team used 132 paired observations of the reference-panel voltage difference and the test module’s power losses to calibrate the cleaning trigger. To assess cleaning performance, the researchers used the test module as its own baseline, comparing power output before and after each of 30 autonomous cleaning cycles under comparable conditions.
“On a 180 W monocrystalline module, average output increased from 93 W under heavily soiled conditions to 173.7 W following cleaning, corresponding to an efficiency improvement of 86.7% and recovery of 93% of soiling-induced power losses across approximately 30 autonomous cycles,” the researchers said. “Cleaning intervals ranged from 4 to 14 days, with dust storms accelerating soiling rates by up to a factor of three and rainfall events naturally extending intervals through partial surface cleansing.”
The academics presented the system in “
A low-cost, data-driven, self-powered robotic system for intelligent PV panel maintenance in water-scarce regions
,” published in
Energy Reports
. The research team included scientists from the Islamia University of Bahawalpur in Pakistan, the University of Shanghai for Science and Technology, Yan’an University, and Shanghai University of Medicine and Health Sciences in China.

title: Heat pump, solar-plus-storage retrofit cuts grid electricity purchases by 17% - pv magazine Global
content:
A research team from the
University of Liège
in Belgium has investigated residential energy renovations and found that adding a 5 kWh battery to a heat pump and rooftop PV system can reduce household grid electricity imports by 17% compared with a configuration without storage.
The findings suggest that residential batteries could help households lower their electricity costs by storing surplus solar generation for use during periods when electricity would otherwise be purchased from the grid.
“We selected a representative Belgian semi-detached home from 708 audited dwellings and calibrated its energy model against four years of measured gas and electricity use,” corresponding author Shady Attia told
pv magazine
. “We found that adding battery storage reduced annual grid electricity purchases from 40.0 kWh/m² with solar alone to 33.2 kWh/m² with a 5 kWh battery. This represents a reduction of 6.8 kWh/m² annually, without changing the amount of electricity generated by the rooftop solar installation.”
“The three solar configurations had exactly the same net annual energy use. Yet adding a 5 kWh battery reduced grid imports by 17% and operational emissions by 14% compared with solar alone,” Attia added. “The annual balance hides when the home draws power from the grid.”
Battery sizing
The researchers also examined whether increasing battery capacity delivers proportional benefits. “The batteries charged only from surplus rooftop solar and discharged to meet household demand,” Attia explained.
The simulations compared 2 kWh and 5 kWh batteries, revealing diminishing carbon savings as storage capacity increased.
“The first 2 kWh of capacity saved 0.43 kg CO₂e per square meter per year. Increasing capacity from 2 to 5 kWh saved a further 0.31, so the carbon benefit per added kWh of capacity had already declined over that range,” Attia said.
Although the figures refer to emissions rather than electricity costs, they raise questions about whether the reduction in grid electricity purchases from additional storage capacity would justify the higher investment.
“At 5 kWh, the home used 95% of its own solar generation, leaving little annual surplus for a larger battery to capture under the same control strategy,” Attia said. “We tested two sizes, so we can show diminishing returns without locating a precise threshold.”
The findings suggest that larger batteries would not necessarily deliver proportional reductions in electricity bills, as their ability to reduce grid imports would remain constrained by the availability of surplus solar generation.
The researchers modeled a battery operating strategy in which storage was charged exclusively with surplus rooftop solar electricity. However, systems operating under dynamic electricity tariffs could potentially generate additional savings by charging during low-price periods and discharging when electricity prices are higher.
Attia said alternative control strategies could also affect battery performance. “A carbon-aware controller could also charge from the grid in low-emission hours, including in winter, provided the difference in emissions intensity is large enough to offset storage losses,” he said.
Heat pumps
The researchers also found that replacing a conventional gas boiler with a heat pump delivered the largest individual reduction in operational carbon emissions.
“Replacing the gas boiler with a heat pump delivered the largest operational carbon reduction, at 67%,” Attia said. “Adding rooftop PV and a 5 kWh battery brought the total reduction to 75%, from 18.46 to 4.64 kg CO₂e per square meter per year.”
However, grid electricity imports remained concentrated in winter and evening periods, when solar generation was insufficient to meet household demand.
Attia said the results depend on the characteristics of individual buildings and their energy systems. “The percentage depends on the dwelling’s heating demand, the fuel being replaced, heat pump efficiency, solar output, and the local grid’s hourly emissions profile,” he said.
The findings show that residential battery storage can reduce grid electricity purchases even when annual net energy consumption remains unchanged. However, the study did not quantify electricity bill savings or investment payback periods.
The researchers presented their findings in “
Decarbonizing residential buildings: Evaluating heat pump solar and battery renovation pathways
,” published in
Applied Energy

title: South Australia cuts rooftop solar after storm sparks power outages - pv magazine Global
content:
The South Australian government has declared a state of emergency after a “significant” storm cell caused catastrophic damage to electricity transmission infrastructure across the Eyre Peninsula and West Coast, interrupting electricity supply to thousands of customers across the region.
“Severe weather on Thursday 19 November 2026 has caused significant damage to electricity transmission infrastructure, including the destruction of two transmission towers on the 132 kV line between Cultana and Port Lincoln,” the declaration says. “The damage has disrupted electricity supply to communities across the central and lower Eyre Peninsula and West Coast.”
Transmission network operator Electranet said about 24,000 customers across the region had lost power. In an update issued on Friday, it said local generation had restored power to many customers but approximately 10,000 properties on the Eyre Peninsula were still in the dark, warning electricity restoration could take several days as emergency crews work to establish backup supply.
South Australia Energy Minister Tom Koutsantonis declared an electricity supply emergency under the Energy Management Act 2004 to support the coordinated response and restoration of electricity supply to affected communities.
The declaration, that will remain in force for 14 days unless revoked earlier, gives the government power to use a diesel generator in Port Lincoln and instructs the Australian Energy Market Operator (AEMO) to “seek spare generation.”
Koutsantonis said ElectraNet and electricity distributor SA Power Networks (SAPN) were working to restore electricity supply as safely and quickly as possible.
The state is also asking households in the Port Lincoln region that have already had their power restored to switch off their
rooftop solar
systems until advised otherwise by SAPN to avoid tripping the temporary generators supplying them.
“Given Pt Lincoln is now “islanded” from the NEM, we are asking people in that region with solar panels to safely turn them off because they could trip the temporary generators supplying the township,” Koutsantonis said.
“Please go to the
SAPN website
and follow the instructions to safely turnoff your solar array. This advice does not apply to rest of the state.”

ElectraNet said its crews are working around the clock to restore transmission services as quickly and safely as possible.
“This involves engineering and constructing temporary solutions to restore transmission supply while the damaged infrastructure is repaired,” it said. “Given the extent of the damage, some communities could remain without power for several days.”
The event has triggered memories of the 2016 blackout when South Australia suffered a statewide blackout.
In that event, a storm damaged critical transmission infrastructure in the state’s Mid North, triggering a cascading failure across the electricity system that caused South Australia to separate from the broader National Electricity Market. Once that interconnection was lost, the system could no longer remain stable and the entire state experienced what is known as a black system event with parts of the state left without power for about three days.
While this event is much more localised, state MP Sam Tefler said it raises plenty of questions about energy security and about ensuring supply.
“There will be many questions to answer once the immediate response and restoration occurs,” he said.

title: Swegon unveils CO2 rooftop heat pump - pv magazine Global
content:
Swedish heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) manufacturer Swegon has unveiled Lambda Zero, a new packaged rooftop air-to-air heat pump designed for heating and cooling applications in large commercial buildings.
“With capacities from 20 to 70 kW, nominal air flow 4.000 to 11.000 m3/h and five configurations, it brings natural refrigerant technology into a new generation of rooftop solutions,” the company said in a statement.
The system is available in cooling-only and heat pump configurations. It uses natural refrigerant R744 (CO2), with a global warming potential (GWP) of 1.
According to the manufacturer, the unit combines an advanced transcritical refrigeration circuit with inverter-driven variable-capacity technology and machine learning-based control algorithms. The configuration is intended to improve seasonal energy efficiency and maintain reliable operation across a wide range of conditions.
Swegon said the system can operate with variable airflow, allowing it to adjust the volume of treated air according to building requirements and reduce unnecessary energy consumption. The product is available in five configurations, with additional accessories for different installation requirements.
The company has also incorporated active thermodynamic heat recovery into versions equipped with three dampers. This feature is designed to recover energy and reduce the consumption associated with conditioning fresh ventilation air.
According to Swegon’s technical brochure, the Lambda Zero Hi range comprises six sizes with nominal cooling capacities of 25 kW to 67 kW, while the reversible Lambda Zero Hi HP version offers heating and cooling capacities spanning approximately 28 kW to 75 kW.
The manufacturer specifies a seasonal energy efficiency ratio (SEER) of up to 5.24 and a seasonal coefficient of performance (SCOP) of up to 3.91.
Swegon claims that its inverter-driven compressor technology can improve SEER by up to 30% and SCOP by up to 10% compared with a conventional compressor configuration. Optional electronically commutated plug fans can further improve seasonal efficiency by up to 8%, according to the company.
The system also supports adaptive defrosting, free cooling, supply-air temperature adjustment and remote monitoring through Modbus RS485 and Ethernet connectivity.
The manufacturer identifies retail stores, shopping malls, exhibition centers, warehouses and industrial buildings as potential applications for the technology.

title: Toshiba launches photovoltaic-output photocoupler for automotive relays - pv magazine Global
content:
Japanese electronics giant
has launched a photovoltaic-output photocoupler for solid-state relays (SSRs) used in automotive equipment. The device uses light from an internal LED to generate a voltage that switches on an external metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor (MOSFET), which controls current flow in the relay.
“Relay units for automotive equipment are required to offer a longer service life, smaller sizes and higher reliability,” the company said in a statement. “The contacts of mechanical relays are subject to wear and contact failure with long-term use, so mechanical relays are increasingly being replaced by SSRs, which have no moving contacts and use semiconductors for switching.”
The new device, dubbed TLX9909, features a series-connected photodiode array illuminated by an infrared LED. At 25 C and an LED input current of 10 mA, it delivers a typical open-circuit voltage of 17.5 V and a typical short-circuit current of 20 µA, with minimum values of 13.5 V and 8 µA, respectively.
“The new product complies with AEC-Q101, the reliability standard for automotive electronic components, and is suitable for SSR applications in automotive equipment such as battery management systems (BMS), on-board chargers (OBC), and inverter units,” the company said.
In December 2023, Toshiba
introduced the TLX9910
, another photovoltaic-output photocoupler designed for solid-state relays in automotive battery management systems, on-board chargers and inverters. The company has also developed
a 2,200 V silicon carbide MOSFET
for solar inverters and energy storage systems, with the aim of reducing equipment size and weight.
